title: PA Contribution to Afghanistan (Flood Response) via Sida Hum Partnership Agrmt
description: This project will transfer funds from the Humanitarian Partnership Agreement (HPA), a multiyear partnership between Oxfam GB and the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida), to Oxfam Novib for use in a flood response project in Afghanistan. Multi -purpose cash (MPC) interventions will be used to enable families to buy food, Non Food Items (NFIs), repair their shelter or to rent a shelter with adequate latrines, water in safe distance and other basic household emergency needs. Beside hygiene promotion activities will complement the ongoing support.

Improvement of OPA capacities to respond to risks and hazards affecting the life of their members and the strengthening of organizational capacities of 5 partners implementing the programme. title: WBI Augmentation Durable des Revenus de Cafeiculteurs/trices dans l'île d'Idjwi
description: The project will have 3 essential components: 1). Increase of added value of the coffee in getting the double certification (bio and fair trade) of the production of 2000 producers; 2). Professionalism of the cooperative CPNCK (Cooperative of National Coffee Producers of Kivu) through the support to constituent bodies and to different committees in order to ensure transparent and effective management for the cooperative to be able to grow and become an economic actor in the Island of Idjwi; 3). Improve the position of coffee producers within the cooperative through access of women to benefits of coffee and participation in decision making around the production and trading of coffee. Expected results: 1). Double certification (bio and fair trade) granted to 2000 coffee producers in 2017; 2) 2000 targeted members of the project are trained in bio and fair trade coffee production. The price for selling coffee for 2000 producers members of the CPNCK increase with a minimum of 60%( from $1,5/kg to $2,5/kg). The cooperative gives the opportunity for seasonal work to 500 members of the targeted community. 2). The functioning of social bodies and Management of the CPNCK is in line with the status (regular meeting of bodies, General Assemblies (once per year), Minutes of meetings and decision acts taken, transparent administrative and financial management towards members. This will be a priority as CHVs play a key role in community mobilisation as well as setting up of community structures eg community health committees. title: Coordination and Support to the DRC Programme
description: he quality of programs is widely recognized within Oxfam as a foundation for the organization's ability to fully achieve its objectives. This is true in many ways: Building quality is, at its core, a learning process, rooted in action and people. Reproducing this unique knowledge into thematic and program management processes is like feeding the engine of a virtuous cycle. Quality is knowledge. It brings a sense of stability and consistency to the programs, a confirmation of the course chosen to keep the ship afloat, no matter what. Quality is stability When it is visible, unequivocal, it helps to build a positive image and a climate of trust necessary to extend the partnership and reach of the organization. Quality is a growth factor. Finally, the added value of a programme that is constantly governed by quality standards translates into increased impact and scale, which in turn translates into a reduction in poverty and injustice, at the heart of Oxfam's ideal. Quality is a strategic lever for impact.

title: Enhancing Disaster Preparedness and capacity for initial rapid response - NorthK
description: In the Horn of Africa, East and Central Africa (HECA) region, more than 47 million people were already food insecure due to the triple crisis of floods, locust invasion and now COVID -19.  According to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC)  - November 2021, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is experiencing one of the worst food crises in the world, with 27 million people, or 26% of the population, experiencing high acute food insecurity. The impact of conflict, the primary cause of food insecurity, is long -lasting.  This project will help reduce the impact of humanitarian disasters by more than 8 million people in phase 3+ of acute food insecurity identified in eastern DRC; with a likely increase of 0.21% by the end of the first half of 2022. The strengthening of basic services and other infrastructure (water, hygiene and sanitation, health and education services within the community) must continue to ensure dignified living conditions and equitable access for all communities. Host areas Internally Displaced Persons (PDIs) are often subject to risks and protection incidents due to cohabitation and promiscuity within host families; support for the process of reconciliation between host communities (displacement or return) will be necessary. Mechanisms for prevention and mitigation of protection risks will need to be put in place. Host communities also need access to information on available humanitarian assistance and communication channels need to be adapted to their preferences. In order to prevent tensions and conflict over land between communities. Support for the restoration and development of basic social services and/or essential infrastructure and economic recovery will be considered for returnees. In particular, it is important to ensure the protection and respect of basic rights of people affected by the crisis, especially for women heads of households with regard to their access to land, and to prevent them from being discriminated

title: Emergency Response Program in Eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC)
description: This new project is a continuation of DRCC05 project linked to the previous Humanitarian Programme Implementation Plan (PIP) (P00884) which ended on March 31, 2022. This project falls under the National Strategic Change Objective 3. It is linked to the Oxfam International (OI) preparedness and response plan. Contributing to reduce the impact of humanitarian disasters to affected people in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) Provinces, this project will increase the effectiveness and timeliness of Oxfam's responses to humanitarian emergencies in DRC through the establishment of an effectively managed and appropriate contingency stock, and setting up an Oxfam Emergency Response Team. The aim of the emergency response programme in the east of the Democratic Republic of Congo is to reduce morbidity and mortality among populations affected by conflict and various disasters (displaced people, disaster victims and host communities) by implementing life -saving activities during the acute phase of emergencies in the east of the DRC (provinces of North Kivu, South Kivu, Tanganyika, Ituri and Maniema), the target being around 800,000 people, 54% of whom will be women. The main activities are around improving access to drinking water and promoting hygiene by building or rehabilitating Water Hygiene and Sanitation(EHA) facilities, providing emergency water supplies and raising people's awareness on best hygiene practices.   In addition, to relieve these same populations in terms of household water storage capacity, Non Food Items(NFI) Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) kits and intimate hygiene kits (for women of childbearing age) will be distributed to the people targeted in the various intervention zones. As part of the project's cross -cutting approach, protection activities will also be carried out, including training (on protection concepts) for various sections of the community and awareness -raising campaigns on protection issues for beneficiary communities.

title: MERCI_Multisectoral Emergency Response for Conflict Impacted population in South
description: This new project is a continuation of the DRCC07 project from the previous Humanitarian Programme Implementation Plan (PIP) (P00884) which closed on March 31, 2022. This project falls under the National Change Objectives (NCOS3). It is linked to the Oxfam International (OI) preparedness and response plan. Contributing to reduce the impact of humanitarian disasters on up to 740 000 affected people in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) Provinces, this project will increase the effectiveness and timeliness of Oxfam's responses to humanitarian emergencies in DRC by establishment of an effectively managed and appropriate contingency stock, and setting up an Oxfam Emergency Response Team. Some key activities will be carried out, including the provision of safe drinking water through the construction of water points; the construction of sanitation facilities with hygiene promotion activities in the project areas; household livelihood support followed by education on the proper use of food. In addition, community protection activities will be carried out.  MERCI, une réponse multisectorielle axée sur la protection, vise à répondre aux besoins de 31 820 personnes (54% de femmes et de filles ; 19 701 enfants dont 14 813 âgés de 5 à 17 ans) touchées par les conflits interethniques dans dix communautés de Bijombo (Bijombo centre, Muranvia, Kajembwe, Mugete, Irango, Mugogo), Katobo (Ndegu et Mashuba), Lemera et Bwegera. L'objectif est d'assurer une réponse humanitaire adéquate, urgente et flexible pour servir les populations récemment déplacées, les populations dans les zones de retour qui ont été partiellement ou complètement détruites, et les communautés hôtes qui connaissent une vulnérabilité importante en raison du conflit et de la pression exercée par les personnes déplacées sur leurs ressources limitées. title: Ebola response 2025-2026 in DRC - Kasai/Bulape
description: In September 2025, the Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo officially declared an Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreak affecting the Bulape Health Zone in Kasai Province. The zone hosts approximately 253,686 spread across 19 health areas with 142 villages, including seven affected health areas (Bulape, Bulape Communautaire, Dikolo, Ingongo, Mpianga, Bambalai, and Mpatambamba). An assessment conducted by Oxfam and the Bulape Health Zone Office from  5–10 October 2025 identified critical humanitarian needs linked to the prevention and control of infection, access to safe water, hygiene, and sanitation, as well as risk communication and community engagement. At health -facility level, the evaluation found severe Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) and Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) gaps undermining the safety of patients and frontline workers. Four out of seven health centres lack triage or isolation areas, and none have functional IPC committees, sterilization units, or adequate stocks of personal protective equipment (PPE). Even for the three that do, the existing infrastructure is not in good condition.  Health staff are insufficiently trained on IPC standards, and most facilities lack standard operating procedures for cleaning, waste segregation, or safe handling of medical materials. All seven facilities face serious water shortages, relying on distant, unprotected sources, with water purchased at 2,000–3,500 Congolese Francs (CDF) per 20 litres. Immediate rehabilitation or construction of seven community water points, storage tanks (2,000 L), and handwashing stations in health facilities is required to ensure safe service delivery. Sanitation conditions are also alarming: most health centres need the construction or rehabilitation of latrines, showers, and seven incinerators and placenta pits  for safe waste disposal.  Oxfam proposes an integrated WASH–Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) and Protection response to the Ebola Virus Disease (EVD)

title: Integrated Resiliency Building -WASH,Food Security Initiatives in South Kivu-DRC

The project will improve access to water for irrigation, consumption and hygiene, boost food production and security, support sustainable livelihoods and promote good practices in health, the environment and nutrition. The project will also contribute to the prevention of zoonotic diseases and the strengthening of protection mechanisms, particularly for women who are victims of gender -based violence. To implement this project, Oxfam will work in financial partnership with two national organisations, APDIK (Farmers' Association for Integrated Development in South Kivu) and JSD (Youth for Solidarity and Development in the Great Lakes Region), as well as government technical services specializing in the project's key sectors.  These two organizations will work closely with Oxfam to contribute to the sustainable strengthening of the resilience of the most vulnerable populations (host and displaced populations, particularly women and girls) exposed to health, food and protection risks in the territories of Mwenga, Walungu and Kabare, South Kivu province,in Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), as part of an integrated ‘ONE HEALTH' approach.  This will be achieved through:  - Improving access to water for field irrigation, consumption and personal hygiene, and enhancing economic security for vulnerable populations in the project's target areas.    - Strengthening resilience and food security by boosting food production and promoting good practices for a balanced diet in the project's target areas   - Preventing and mitigating the impact of epidemics, diseases and zoonoses (Mpox) in the project's target areas through ‘One Health' best practices.  - Supporting referral systems to improve access to healthcare services for women who are victims of Gender Based Violence

description: - Implementation by the producers of sustainable and profitable peanut & cassava production systems;  - Rehabilitation and operationalisation of a cassava processing plant in Bayaha / Malféty, Fort Liberte commune;  - Sustainable management of processing units by community -based organizations as a basis for development of local production (cassava and peanut);  - Strengthening grassroots organizations in their ability to develop local services (BIA + nurseries)

title: Urban Reconstruction project in the Desprez area, Haiti
description: This project aims at improving living conditions of the vulnerable urban population in Port -au -Prince, in particular in the neighbourhood of Desprez, in the Carrefour Feuilles area. PARAD links economic and social strengthning to infrastructure improvement (roads, corridors, Water Sanitation and Hygiene, ravines, retaining walls...). This projects builds on local participation both in planning and implementation.

title: Household Eonomic Approach study, Haiti
description: The overall objective is to achieve economic analysis of households in OXFAM intervention areas in the upper Artibonite, North and North -East, namely rural communes of Anse Rouge, Ferrier, Ranquitte and La Victoire, these Household Economic Approach  will make a clear contribution to the actual severe drought.

title: Private Banking Sector-Humanitarian Preparedness and Response to Disasters,HAITI
description: Oxfam and the Unibank Foundation are proposing to develop a network and  tools that will be set up and ready before a crisis and therefore ready to deliver quickly and with a clear capacity to design appropriate modalities with a prior understanding of emergency response requirements and design needs.

title: Improved food and nutrition security through agriculture & agroforestry, Haiti
description: The project has two components and will be executed by our partner CLES. CLES will continue to work with local producers following the approach of strengthening MUSOs and implementation of organic vegetable gardens. Through this project, Oxfam intends to: 1 -Fund the production of vegetables through organized local producers (based on past experience with CLES); 2 -Introduce new farming techniques in the area  et 3 -Mobilize the communities on the effects of climate change in order to increase their ability to adapt.

title: Social mobilisation in the Cap-Ouanaminthe corridor through radio novelas, Haiti
description: As reinforcement to current projects and to reach a wider audience with a higher impact, Oxfam wants to develop a "radio novella"  programme. Through the development of a plot line and characters, it will include the key messages from our various projects (violence against women, cholera, disaster risk reduction, climate change, nutrition and waste management ). This is an effective and innovative way of disseminating messages with an attempt to change behaviour, attitudes and knowledge as people are usually quickly captivated by the stories, characters and begins debates on important issues raised during the series.

title: Investment and Research Development Fund
description: Invest in research and development of current programme and the sequence.

title: Economic & social inclusion of marginalized people in border trade zones, Haiti
description: The project contributes to the reduction of poverty of the marginalized informal sector cross -border shopping areas by promoting their access to sustainable livelihoods and better social inclusion.   It will also ensure organizational strengthening of marginalized interest groups, ownership of their rights, extending the coverage of social protection, support for entrepreneurship and the creation of productive jobs around the bi -national markets Haïti -Republique Dominicaine.

title: Reduction of food insecurity by improving resilience of vulnerable populations
description: To strengthen resilience (absorption, adaptation and transformation) of the population to shocks in the food systems, by better management of food crises and support to integrated local and territorial development, in particular the capacities of public institutions and communities to manage 1) food crises, including early warning, targeting and contingency planning; 2) local social and economic development, in particular nutrition and social protection; and 3) integrated water resources management (IWRM) and natural resources management

title: PA Discretionary Contribution in Haiti FY2018
description: The project support Oxfam and partners capacity to implement resilience, influencing and bi -national initiatives (with Dominican Republic) aiming at improving economical and social conditions of vulnerable groups in Haiti. Resources will be invested to leverage donor funding and support partners, local governments and Oxfam in the implementation and scaling up of projects targeting food security, water resource management, economic development and national and international advocacy on bi -national  such as migration, disaster risk reduction, access to social services and value chains.

title: Economic & social inclusion of marginalized people in border trade zones, Haiti
description: This project comes from HAIC99  - a UE multi year and multi -affiliate funded project lead by Oxfam Italy. The project covers the bi - national zone and started in 2016 -2017 and ends in 2018 -2019.

title: PA Contribution to Haiti FY19 to FY21
description: Development of a Women Rights and Gender Justice Program Creation of a global Monitoring Evaluation and Accountability and Learning (MEAL) strategy for the mission which takes into account Women rights and Gender Justice issues Develop a Funding Strategy for Haiti, maximise fundraising and ensure grant management for the mission  - particular attention on Women rights and Gender Justice issues

title: Right to a Future for People Affected by the Syrian Displacement Crisis
description: The Theory of Change posits that people affected by the protracted Syrian displacement crisis – either as displaced persons or host communities  - will realise their ‘right to a future' and live dignified lives (impact), if they have security, voice, access to quality basic services, and safe and sustainable livelihoods (ultimate outcome). This ultimate outcome is achievable when developed countries share greater responsibility, including through funding and provision of international protection, for supporting displaced persons and host communities (outcome 1); governments from refugee -hosting countries in the region have the capacity and political will to uphold the basic rights of vulnerable displaced and host communities (outcome 2); and displaced and host communities' voices are heard and acted upon by duty bearers in development planning (outcome 3). To contribute to these outcomes, this project will support the capacity and space for civil society organisations in Lebanon, and at the international level, to influence national and international duty bearers to more effectively meet the needs of both vulnerable displaced and host communities through the ‘resilience agenda', including by raising the voices of affected populations, policy monitoring, research, coalition -building and innovation.

title: WaSH, Protection and Livelihood response to the Syria Crisis in Lebanon
description: Oxfam's response will be an integrated WASH, Livelihood and Protection intervention benefitting 8,793 individuals (adjusted for double counting), including refugees and poor Lebanese where appropriate. Oxfam will deliver WASH in informal settlements and camps in North Bekaa, where Livelihood activities will also be prioritized. Protection activities will be implemented in North, West and Central Bekaa. The project has three immediate outcomes as reflected in the Logic Model and Performance Measurement Framework. The project aims to enable Oxfam to start transitioning into longer term, cost effective and sustainable (where possible) approach to providing humanitarian assistance in the context of a protracted crisis and increasingly restrictive government policies on refugees.

title: Building Alternative Development Assets and Entrepreneurial Learning in Lebanon
description: If Lebanese, Palestinian, and Syrian community members and relevant stakeholders in targeted communities have an enhanced understanding of resilience assets to conflict and vulnerability, in addition to the available socio -economic opportunities, and if locally owned and driven innovative solutions are advanced with the skills, tools, and expertise for successful impact and sustainability, then social stability is protected, community (hosting and refugee populations) participation advanced, and civic engagement strengthened. This change will contribute to countering drivers of conflict and radicalisation and bolster resilience  through civic activism and participation.

title: Cash for Work for Donnieh's Vulnerable population, North Lebanon
description: The overall objective of the project is to contribute to the strengthening of social stability in vulnerable Lebanese Municipality. The project will help reduce the strain on public resources and infrastructure, due to over -exploitation and competition in access between refugee communities and host communities. In doing so, then the project will help strengthen the resilience of local communities and social cohesion of the same. In fact, the rehabilitation of spaces and public infrastructure will support the municipalities in land management. In addition, the increase in access to income -generating activities for the population, although for a limited period of time, reduce the risk of resorting to negative coping mechanisms for the families of the beneficiaries of temporary employment schemes. The rehabilitation of public spaces will increase community access to meeting places which, in turn, will help to reduce social tensions due to the consequences of the Syrian crisis

title: Increased access to water and dignified lives to vulnerable people in Lebanon
description: Oxfam will equip refugees with key information pertaining to their access to essential services and civil status documentation. Oxfam, through its partnership with specialised local Sexual and Gender Based Violence (SGBV) case management organisations, addresses systematically the needs of women within the community. Oxfam will support the most vulnerable with immediate, one -time cash assistance, while referring them to relevant services. In parallel, Oxfam, through specialised micro -finance partners, seeks to contribute to households' autonomous coping mechanisms through individual coaching on income saving and, where appropriate, facilitate the establishment of communal savings groups, which give their members a safety net against destabilising life events.

title: Addressing extreme vulnerabilities among refugees and HC in Lebanon
description: - Provide 4 months temporary cash assistance to 2500 vulnerable Lebanese and Syrian refugee households  - Service Mapping for Lebanese households   - Capacity -building of one Social Development Centre on cycle management for cash assistance and for referrals   - Community awareness sessions on access to protection referral services and to help and inform women to counter Gender Based Violence (GBV)  - Support 4 new and existing community structures (women and youth groups) to safely identify and refer community members to protection actors and service providers when needed  - Improve access to protection services and provide specialised protection services 141 Syrian refugees requiring legal counselling or legal assistance and representation, and specialised case management for Sexual/Gender Based Violence (S/GBV) survivors;   - Produce 8 regular & brief policy products on the emerging protection concerns that negatively impact the most vulnerable communities, with a particular focus on the vulnerability of women in these communities  - Develop a research and influencing products and activities reviewing the national social protection systems that negatively impact the living conditions of communities in Lebanon  - Support community groups and local partners in local advocacy initiatives in order to strengthen advocacy activities on a local level.

title: Strengthened Protection and Resilience of Crisis-affected in Lebanon
description: Oxfam's interventions in Lebanon focus on basic service provision that grants refugees life -sustaining access to clean water and sanitation on the one hand, and empowering their communities to identify, process, and address daily protection concerns on the other, all the while highlighting those concerns and gaps in assistance and rights provision to local authorities and key international stakeholders through its advocacy efforts. In the coming years, this approach would prove even more relevant, as refugees are increasingly compelled to make radical decisions about their future  - like returning to Syria or moving to ostensibly more welcoming areas in Lebanon – with often little reliable information to guide those choices. Oxfam's interventions thus focus on equipping refugees with key information pertaining to their access to essential services, civil status documentation, and rights and protective laws against exploitation and coercion. Information shared with target population will increase the knowledge on own rights, existing legal requirements and ways to access relevant services and assistance available in a safe manner, increasing capacity to prevent and mitigate protection risks. With this knowledge, individuals are also expected to be able to contact service providers directly, through the support of a focal point, or by contacting Oxfam staff and partners. Refugee women, often more vulnerable to abuse and harassment, face unique threats that Oxfam, through its partnership with specialized local SGBV case management organizations, addresses systematically within its broader response to the needs of the community. Oxfam's protection monitoring findings, as well as feedback communicated to its staff in the field, highlight fears of forced return and eviction as being the most preoccupying for refugees. Evictions, in particular, are serious shocks with deep ramifications to refugees' sense of safety and stability. Although evidence suggests that those who

title: MAKANI, MY PLACE.Economic development, decent work and social inclusion, Tripoli
description: the project seeks to promote multi -stakeholder partnerships to identify and promote innovative systems for inclusive economic development: training, entrepreneurial support, service networks, protection of workers' rights, promotion of new opportunities for young people and reactivation of traditional economic sectors.

title: Beirut Explosion Response, Lebanon
description: Overall Objective: Save lives, reduce suffering and enhance resilience of vulnerable groups in Lebanon who have been impacted by the Beirut explosion through a targeted, localised response that will address the root causes of crisis while saving lives in the short term.   Specific Objective 1: Delivery of immediate, quality, safe and inclusive, life -saving emergency assistance to those most impacted community members living in affected areas, including areas outside of Beirut.  Specific Objective 2: Provide coordinated and integrated economic support to affected micro and small enterprises and employees, focusing on the most vulnerable groups, within Beirut and across the country   Specific Objective 3: Contribute to the advancement of Oxfam's Local Humanitarian Leadership approach and principled partnering practice through the Beirut response

title: Promoting Youth Economic Empowerment in Lebanon and Decent work
description: The project seeks to foster young women and men' fair economic participation promoting long -term investments in creativity and innovation in Northern Lebanon.

title: COVID-19 Response -Lebanon -WASH, Protection and Food Security
description: Outcome 1: Improved Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) standards in Informal Settlements (ISs) in North Bekaa, in line with COVID -19 prevention, isolation and quarantine guidelines. The proposed WASH intervention will focus on emergency WASH activities (life -saving WASH services). The WASH activities will be implemented through a safe programming approach with the involvement of affected communities. This will be done in close coordination with the two municipalities.  Accordingly, WASH activities will reach 4,746 Syrian refugees (2,310 women; 2,436 men) in 93 ISs in Saaide and Bouday. The nature of the WASH intervention will depend on the isolation guidance levels. Outcome 2: Improved access by refugees, especially women and girls, to reliable and comprehensive information on COVID -19 prevention Oxfam's initial response to COVID -19 was to engage communities. Ensuring trusted and two -way communication channels is a top priority in the current situation and moving forward, so that communities can receive and share information and engage in developing solutions to challenges being raised. Based on the initial discussions, questions raised were prioritized and addressed in the form of Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs), thereby contextualizing the COVID -19 information on the most ‘need -to -know' basis, in addition to besides the WASH and Health sectors' agreed messaging. Given the protracted nature of the humanitarian response in Lebanon; the response had mostly transitioned to a cash -based response in line with Grand Bargain commitment to "increase the use and coordination of cash -based programming." However, given the mobility challenges that the COVID -19 crisis brings on refugee communities to access cash, coupled with the ongoing challenges of the banking sector in Lebanon due to the economic and financial situation; as part of the COVID -19 response strategy, Lebanon Crisis Response Plan (LCRP) partners are asked to prepare for likely food distribution f

title: Promotion of decent work and sustainable business development in Bekaa, Lebanon
description: Support Local CSOs to increase awareness on labour rights and decent work, train business development support organisations, and support MSMEs. At the same time, support the business environment in Bekaa to recover and develope.

title: SEE_Social Entrepreneurship Ecosystem- Change, Leb
description: If community awareness on SE and social economy is further developed; if financial and non -financial support to existing and start -up SEs are provided to contribute to their sustainability and scale -up; if tailored capacity development is provided to SESOs; and if support to local networks working on SE policy is continued, then, social stability opportunities will be created, and the local social economy will be supported.

title: "WASTE OR RESOURCE? – Environmental and social responsibility of municipalities
description: R1: to respond to the problem of insufficient or poorquality separate collection, a separate collection management system will be introduced in Hasbaya and Chebaa, the two largest towns in the district, and the separate collection plan, already present in Rashaya Al Foukhar, will be revised. The new plans will be co -designed, implemented and monitored, ensuring both adequate technical and management training and the supply of vehicles and containers. In order for the separate collection systems to work, an awareness campaign will be designed and implemented for the correct separation and disposal of waste at domestic and commercial level. Finally, separate collection plans will be developed and presented and peer to peer trainings will be organized for the 9 municipalities not involved in the implementation of the service to ensure that they will have all the tools to implement the plans. R2: to improve waste treatment, which is currently insufficient, 3 composting centres in Hasbaya, Chebaa and Rashaya Al Foukhar and 2 recyclables sorting centres in Hasbaya and Chebaa will be built. The centres will be designed, built and equipped with the necessary machinery; the operators will then be trained at a technical and management level and a management model and system for monitoring the functioning of the centres will be developed; finally, an endowment fund will be established for the start -up of the Hasbaya and Chebaacentres. To improve waste disposal, which is currently inadequate, the environmental impacts of the existing open dumpsites in Hasbaya, Chebaa and Rashaya Al Foukhar will be mitigated: the waste already present will be contained and covered and new lots and plans will be prepared for the controlled disposal of unsorted waste; dumpsites operators will be trained and monitored to correctly implement the new procedures and analyses will be carried out to assess the environmental impacts. Finally, treatment and disposal plans will be elaborated and presente

title: Qadreen: Generating temporary employment opportunities for the most vulnerable
description: Contribute to mitigating the social consequences of the Syrian crisis and the economic crisis on the most vulnerable groups in the Minieh -Donnieh district.  Improve access to income and better infrastructure and public services for vulnerable refugees and Lebanese in Minieh -Donnieh district, reducing social tensions.  The present project revolves around the following theory of change:    If vulnerable men and women have access to opportunities for temporary employment in productive public infrastructure and environmental protection in the municipalities of  Bqarsouna and Bqaa Sifrine (R1) , and community -based services are provided at municipal level in Bqarsouna and Bqaa Sifrine (R2) and integrated municipal solid waste management  services are improved in Bqaa Sifrine  to reduce social tensions (R3), then access to income and better infrastructure and public services for refugees and vulnerable Lebanese in Minieh -Donnieh district will be increased, reducing social tensions.

title: South Emergency Response
description: - Generation of knowledge on Renewable Energy   - Renewable Energy Projects for scaling   - Food Security and Agricultural linkages under the Nexus Approach   - Piloting alternative and sustainable Menstrual Products   - Group Cash Transfers   - Support to Migrant Communities   - Lebanon Water Forum

title: B-READY Global Scale-up: Planning Grant (Lebanon)
description: Oxfam proposes to embark on a new strategic partnership to scale Building Resilient, Adaptive and Disaster Ready Communities (B -READY): an innovation uniting parametric disaster climate forecasting with financial inclusion to provide social protection to individuals, communities, and businesses in advance of emergencies.

title: UNDP Supporting a Feminist Socio-Economic Working Group
description: • Formation of the Feminist Socio -Economic Working Group (FSEWG): A working group comprised of women activists, economists, researchers, and policy analysts. • Influencing activities: Research, policy recommendations, and advocacy efforts will be conducted jointly with the FSEWG.

title: Lebanon Response IDP South
description: supporting IDPs with basic needs such as water and MHM kits

title: LABNE - Local Agriculture Governance to Boost iNnovative  Economic Models
description: Support to the Dairy Sector through UOMs and The Chamber of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture of Tripoli and North Lebanon (CCIAT) and Ministry of Agriculture (MOA) for Farmers, Agri Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) and Job seekers.

title: Cooperative development and women's economic empowerment in cotton areas of Mali
description: This project will develop autonomous cooperatives in cotton areas of southern Mali, via provision of training, extension support, equipment and finance to enable diversification and more sustainable production practices, supported by national advocacy to improve the policy framework and rural investment. Economic activities of women will be promoted as well as measures to enable improved literacy, security of land tenure and access to finance for this group, which in turn will increase their access to decision making at local level.

title: Strengthening the cotton programme beneficiaries to adapt to climate change
description: The Malian National Action Plan of Adaptation to climate change highlights the high vulnerability of rural small farmers who constitute main beneficiaries of the Oxfam Cotton programme. Beyond the need to understand the nature of this vulnerability and to make an assessment of the possible adaptation options, this project of research -development will lead to a better information, education and communication campaign on climate change and its adverse effects. This project will also experiment in the best sustainable practices on adaptation to climate change such as mutual insurance, early mature crop seeds and water harvesting.

title: R&D project to strengthen baseline analysis on Food Security in the Sahel
description: The overall objective of the project is to increase the ability of Oxfam GB to better respond to recurrent  food crisis in Gao, north of Mali.  The adopted strategies are investment in analysis and human resources.  The results coming out of the major research activity of the project, the Household Economy Analysis (HEA) supplemented by the Cost of the Diet, are going to be used as baseline data for future programming and proposal development.

title: Integrated Water - Education in Gao Region, Mali
description: In 2007/2008 the Ministry of Education reported that in Gao regions rates of enrolment were 96.1%. In Gao region, poor health and child malnutrition rates are alarmingly high. A lack of safe drinking water, inadequate sanitation facilities and poor health awareness, as well as inadequate access to education facilities all contributes. This project aims to improve access to clean water for school children and local villagers and improve the learning environment in the poorest. Its a continuing project during 4 years.

title: Water, Sanitation, and Public Health Promotion in Gao, Mali
description: Malnutrition will be reduced in the Gao region, through the promotion of appropriate technologies for water supply and sanitation. Good hygiene and nutrition practices are being promoted as part of this project, as well as integrated water resources management, to ensure sustainability.  Twenty -four villages (42000 people) in the communes of Bamba and Temera will benefit. Promising low cost technologies, (hand -augered tubewells and rope and washer pumps), introduced during the first phase of Bani Fonda, will be scaled up and promoted.  An advocacy strategy will be prepared and implemented.

title: Increasing Food Security in Mali
description: Oxfam GB in partnership with Save the Children US and the Institute of Rural Economics proposes an action that aims to globally reinforce resilience capacity of the poorest rural population to cope with the rising food prices, therefore contributing to fight against hunger in Mali. The project will target specifically poor and very poor households in the regions of Gao and Sikasso to enhance and secure access to food. It involves direct actions (cash transfers, sale subsidy of animal fodder, seeds production, regeneration of the pasture, trainings, etc), a Household Economy Analysis, results learning & dissemination and advocacy.

title: Empowering women in agricultural markets through collective action
description: This project will generate new evidence on rural women's effective collective action in agricultural markets in Mali, to improve practice in Oxfam and partners' programmes.  In  Koulikoro and Sikasso regions, and nationally, stakeholder dialogues will other communication channels will engage key actors and promote evidence based innovation.   Funding for the initiative is secured from Gates Foundation.

title: Emergency Response to Food Crisis in Northern Mali
description: This project aims to mitigate the current critical food insecurity of extremely vulnerable agro -pastoralist and pastoralist households affected by agriculture gazing land, water and fodder deficit in the Gao region through targeted free distribution of food and aliment feed throughout the hunger gap. This is the second emergency response in Mali within the year, as the interventions and policies are not relevant to the crisis and can't have a long term impact. This project will have a communication and advocacy component to make sure that there is enough coordination and appropriate actions from the donors and the government. SCO3.1.

title: Improving access to safe water for populations affected by the food crisis Mali
description: The project will be implemented with the close participation of local authorities (at regional, district and communal levels) and relevant technical departments from the various sectors. Intervention areas are targeted considering the ongoing interventions by other international organisations involved in the Gao region, such as Action Contre la Faim – Espagne, SNV, AEN, ICRC, etc. as well as UN agencies such as FAO, WFP, UNICEF and government agencies such as the Commissariat à la Sécurité Alimentaire (CSA), the Système d'Alerte Précoce (SAP). Interventions modalities will also be determined in light of current successful practices

title: Reduce the vulnerability of households and communities in Gao Region
description: This project is for the response to the food crisis in Temera and Taboye communes in Gao, where we have the most households affected by the bad agriculture campaign of 2011 -2012 as well as the greatest number of returnees from Libya. From this project, 2,200 households will benefit from unconditional cash transfers and cash for work activities. 100 women groups will be targeted by the sensitisation activities and training on malnutrition risk prevention. 100 members from livestock cooperatives will participate in sensitisation and capacity building on livestock destocking.

title: Humanitarian Response to the Food Crisis in Kayes, Mali
description: This project is set to launch the Oxfam International (OI) response to the food crisis in Kayes. It aims to help mitigate the risks and shocks of the food insecurity in the most vulnerable communities in Kayes region. The response focuses on 3 phases:  - One aiming at strengthening resilience and avoiding the depletion of the livelihoods assets of the very poor and poor families;   - one during the lean period  aiming at increasing the access to food and the fight against malnutrition;  - and an early recovery of the most vulnerable families.  Advocacy, coordination and monitoring complete these actions.

title: Capitalizating experiences on food crops and diversification in Mali
description: The project aims to set up a sustainable network of professionals working in the area of social sciences to share experiences and generate a collective knowledge on of food security in cotton producing areas of western and central Africa. More specially, this will be achieved through: creating analytical capitalization tools; communicating widely on the tools; training on scientific publication; diffusion of project findings; and finally creating a discussion space between researchers and practitioners. This project continues from MLIA51.

title: Communicate, Account and Research for Evaluation (CARE)
description: This to design a project that will look at quality of Oxfam intervention in Mali with the underlying hypothesis that "Oxfam is using the opportunity of SMS to acheiving greater and better impacts from its interventions by 2015

title: Food and nutrition security in Kolondieba district, Sikasso region
description: The project aims to improve the nutritional status of children and women in reproductive age through the following activities: i) provision of agricultural inputs and training to poor households for cereal and vegetable production; ii) targeted cash transfer and advice to women belonging to very poor households; iii) awareness raising and training of community advisors and women on nutritional practices; iv) support to women's groups in processing and conditioning enriched cereal products. Advocacy at local and national level will aim to share good practicies in particular about social protection measures.

title: Advocacy for Food Security in Mali
description: Component 1: support exchange and learning among farmers' organisations on best practices, capacity building for advocacy, institutional support to rural women' organisations, support to initiatives of policy analysis and advocacy on food security by national farmers' organisations.  Component 2: participation in relevant networks in Mali about food security, social protection and disaster risk management, analytical work on policies and practices, capitalisation of experiences at local level for advocacy at national level, link with similar initiatives at regional level

title: Recovery and resilience in Kayes and Yelimane districts
description: The project will contribute to a sustainable improvement of food and nutrition security of 5000 poor and very poor households in the districts of Kayes and Yelimane affected by the food crisis in 2012. The project is a continuation of MLIA90 that accounted for the response to the food crisis in Kayes. This project will now take up the recovery phase for the most vulnerable households affected by the crisis, and will subsequently help them improve their resilience.

title: Mitigate humanitarian crisis for the most vulnerable households in southern Mali
description: This project aims at meeting the most vulnerable households' needs resulting from the recent Mali food and security crises, as well as cholera outbreak. This will be achieved through a) strengthening the resilience capacity of the vulnerable households; b) increasing the access to food (both for human and animal consumption); c) promoting the early recovery and the transition towards longer term livelihoods activities; d) improving communities' access to essential services; and e) increasing the local authorities' capacity to respond to cholera outbreaks when these occur.

title: Humanitarian response to the consequences of the conflict in Mali - 2013
description: The project aims at mitigating the impact of the conflict on vulnerable women, men, girls and boys, by preventing food insecurity and promoting livelihoods recovery and community resilience. This will be achieved through an integrated response that combines Emergency Food Security Livelihood (EFSL), Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Protection and Gender activities.

title: Response to the outbreak of the disease Ebola in Mali
description: Strengthening of hygiene and sanitation capacities of 150 schools in area at risk of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) through:   - Supplying schools with hygiene kits (an average of 3 kits per school according to the utilization rate)  - Provision of hand washing areas (average of 3 areas per schools according to the utilization rate)   - Provision of awareness tools to schools ‘actors: images boxes, flyers for the prevention of EVD will be given to actors in Sensitization of population living in the area prone to EVD on preventive methods of EVD  - Display of sensitization banners and distribution of flyers (large scale distribution of sensitization flyers and banners to be displayed in the schools entrances)  - Training of community relays  - Mass Sensitization (to reach a larger number of people living in the area at risk will be reached through, sketches and social mobilization campaigns)

title: Contribute to strengthen the capacities of resilience of communities in crisis
description: Oxfam is aiming to provide an integrated humanitarian, recovery and resilience response to vulnerable populations in Sikasso, Kayes, Mopti, Tombouctou, Gao, Menaka and Kidal. Our plan is to reach more than 200,000 persons with direct assistance by providing services and goods regarding food security and livelihoods, Water Sanitation and Hygiene and Protection.

title: Revelantly Resourcing & Systematising Program Quality for Better Impact in Mali
description: Look at quality of Oxfam's intervention in Mali under  hypothesis that our work will achieve greater and better impact. The project will ensure an integrated Monitoring Evaluation and Accountability and Learning (MEAL) for Country Program (Resilience, Essential services and Governance programmes) using Common Approach to MEL and Social Accountability (CAMSA) minimum requirements to achieve better quality in programming and monitoring. Capacity building, Program Quality Review, learning events, partnership review and effective MEAL standards within all Oxfam's programmes will be assured. The specific objective of the project is to ensure that Oxfam operates in an environment recognized to be accountable.

title: Emergence of Women Leaders and Support to their Livelihoods.
description: This project aims at facilitating and ensuring women emerging leaders able to influence and create a favourable environment to women and girls to know and benefit for their economic, political and social rights in Sikasso and Goa regions.   This will be possible through :  - Women organised at community level and are able to identify their problems and their needs, look for appropriate solutions and ask for necessary support in case of need.  - Emerging women leaders from community level having good knowledge of the rights of women and girls and are engaged in all spheres of decisions   - Establishment of strong women networks at community level able to advocate and influence politics and practices favourable to Malian women and girls in all levels.  These networks will enable linkages with organisations or associations in rural areas and urban or peri urban areas to facilitate a synergy in action for women and girls.

title: Supporting sustainable  livelihoods and agricultural politics in Mali
description: This project will be implemented in the following  areas; regions of Koulikoro (County of Koulikoro and Nara); Régions of  Segou (county of Segou, and Niono), Region of Sikasso ( county of Sikasso and  Koutiala).  It aims to reach 8456 farmers among which 2540 women farmers and will indirectly impact on 10,000  farmers

title: Strengthening Local Community capacity for their participation indecision making
description: PSEC Project will strengthen groups and associations of women and young people in their internal resource mobilization activities (EPC), while providing support in their production and pastoral activity, follow -up and support for groups of young people and women in the management of their affairs. Also the project envisages the capacity building of grassroots community organizations to influence at the grassroots level the decisions that affect their lives. To achieve this, national and regional advocacy actions will be carried out.

title: Reversing Land Degradation in Mali by scaling up Evergreen Agriculture
description: The project will be implemented in 2 circles (Koutiala and Yorosso) and will be partnering with 3 other organizations working in different areas and Oxfam, as the lead. We will have a strong partnership with technical services on the ground, working on agriculture, forestry. To achieve our objectives, we will use 2 types of interventions, the Direct and the indirect. The direct will be through our field staff and partners work which will reach 12.500 Household and 50,000 ha. The indirect will be through our influencing work to engage other actors on the question of regreening. This indirect intervention will then help to get another 7,000 households and 15,000 ha.    The main a activities will be around building the capacity of farmers, on Trees' production and planting, farmers managing natural regeneration, non timber forest products

title: Support programme for the development of family farming in Mali
description: This project is a continuation of MLIB17 with main objective is to increase income, as well as the  strengthening the power to act and influence of 1600 women enrolled in 3 value chains: Milk, Rice and Soya,  in the region of Koulikoro, Koutiala and Segou.

title: Accountable Local Governance Programme, Phase 2 in Mali
description: The project aims to strengthen the social contract between actors through inclusive governance of local public affairs through training on decentralisation, good governance, conflict management, gender and social inclusion, capacity building of local authorities and advocacy for a better consideration of the needs of youth and women in the plans and budgets of their commune 2400 young people including 1200 women and 80 communal councils will be direct beneficiaries of the project in the 80 communes of the Mopti, Bandiagara and Douentza region.

title: Reversing Land Degradation in Mali by scaling up Evergreen Agriculture
description: Just to specify that this project is a continuation of MLIB16. MLIB27 has been created as MLIB16 can't be extended as the start date of the new Programme Implementation Plan (PIP) it's linked to is set to January 22 . Otherwise there is no other change between MLIB16 and MLIB27.  The project will be implemented in 2 circles (Koutiala and Yorosso) and will be partnering with 3 other organizations working in different areas and Oxfam, as the lead. We will have a strong partnership with technical services on the ground, working on agriculture, forestry. To achieve our objectives, we will use 2 types of interventions, the Direct and the indirect. The direct will be through our field staff and partners work which will reach 12.500 Households and 50, 000 ha. The indirect will be through our influencing work to engage other actors on the question of regreening. This indirect intervention will then help to get another 7,000 households and 15,000 ha. The main activities will be around building the capacity of farmers, on Trees' production and planting, farmers managing natural regeneration, non timber forest products

title: Promoting Learning and Knowledge management in Mali
description: Oxfam in Mali has adopted the common approach of Monitoring Evaluation and Social Accountability CAMSA since 2015 allowing it to put in place a Monitoring Evaluation plan of quantitative data and an accountability system to collect feedback from partners However, one of the great challenges we face is to make learning both a process of performance measurement and knowledge management by which we explain and appreciate the changes obtained, as well as the intervention strategy, with a view to improving the quality of our work, ensuring its relevance, enhancing mutual accountability and strengthening our legitimacy. Through capacity building on learning  - The project is planned for a duration of 6 months and the main activities will revolve around:  - Capacity building on learning for Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) and stakeholders  - Review and capitalization and sharing workshops on cases of learning success (humanitarian action and economic justice and governance component)

title: Assessment for potential specific commodities for PWEL project
description: This project's proposed activities are for consolidation of OGB presence in Thazi township, for building good reputation of OGB, for building effective relation with local authorities and community, for piloting and testing options with a focus on poor women economic leadership (PWEL) which are the foundation of community led food security and livelihoods based capacity building project.  The project will set the basis for definition and consolidation of implementation strategy for the next 12 months.

title: Facilitating a responsible operational exit from Nargis affected communities
description: The project will work with VDCs established in all 43 villages under post -Nargis livelihoods recovery work. It de -emphasises the role of these bodies in receiving & managing assistance & material assets. Rather this project will emphasise our role in facilitating a broader governance mandate of the groups and the role they can play in relating more effectively within & between villages and with the relevant government & private sector service providers. It also sets out deliberately to assist staff to recognise the skills acquired over time & provide them with space to document experiences and understanding their role in facilitating change.

title: Community Centred Development, Pauk Township
description: This project scales up a pilot to establish institutions bringing citizens & local authorities (Las) together. Facilitating the expansion of township coordination structures to include CBO representation will build understanding, greater relevance and transparency to township planning, budgeting & operations. CBOs will be strengthened to ensure they have the abilities to represent their communities effectively. Promoting women in representational roles will challenge stereotypes and barriers to effective governance at the village level. Livelihood activities will be implemented as a platform to constructive dialogue between communities & LAs

title: Disinfection using hydrogen peroxide to support the LLH of water vendors in DDY
description: The innovation will improve the livelihoods of water vendors in Dedaye town through the introduction to the local market of a new form of disinfection. Vendors will sell treated water with sufficient residual hydrogen peroxide levels to withstand re -contamination by poor water use and hygiene practices thus ensuring ‘safe' water at the point of consumption without the need for significant behaviour change. Vendors will also develop a new market for Sanosil treatments amongst those who collect their own water. A market chain for Sanosil will be established and the profit from sales will significantly increase the income of vendors.

title: Improving Food Security and Livelihoods
description: The project will aim to provide strategic support and guidance for the FSWG to deliver meaningful services to the members as well as grow its position as a leading network for advocacy and policy direction.

title: Emergency Response to Flash Floods in Magway Region, Myanmar
description: Flash floods in Magway Division in the heart of Myanmar's Dry Zone caused serious destruction in four townships, as well as loss of life and livelihoods. This is an extremely poor and marginal area, where the population is unused and has very limited capacities to cope with the impacts of acute disasters. The objective of this project is to contribute to restoring immediate food security and a safe public health environment in two affected townships of Magway region, and to facilitate the transition into early recovery and the building of community resilience to disasters.

title: Maximising opportunities for livelihood recovery in Kyaukpyu Township
description: Oxfam and BLO propose additional interventions covering the period between the 2011 monsoon pre -harvest and the preparation and initiation of the 2012 monsoon season (April -May).  In addition to specific results anticipated, all elements are designed to increase continuity and maximise recovery potential.         Small -scale pilots and action research increases understanding and uptake of technical improvements associated with documented gains in consolidating early recovery for small -holder farmers in Kyauk Phyu.

title: Multi-agency planning and analysis - Rakhine
description: Work will be done in collaboration to extend collective understanding (inc sub -regional specifics) crucial to development in the area.  It includes an inventory of damage to key infrastructure necessary for agricultural production, an analysis of fruit production and market opportunities and initiating a consistent and efficient food security analysis system as the basis for an effective FS EWS.  With in this, we will ensure adequate attention is paid to the analysis of gender relations and conduct action research assessing good practice in partnerships between local and international NGOs as a basis for future ways of working.

title: Supporting Regional Department of Agriculture in Dry Zone, Myanmar
description: To support Regional DoA producing hybrid rice seed able to distribute local small -holder farmers   To extend the linkages between farmers and service providers DoA to access improved agriculture technology  To sustain the quality seed productivity in the region to meet DoA targets

title: Tat Lan Rakhine State, Livelihoods recovery and governance
description: The Tat Lan Programme, implemented by the International Rescue Committee (IRC) in partnership with Save the Children UK (SC), Oxfam, and Better Life Organisation (BLO), will build on the emergency response and contribute to equitably and sustainably improving the livelihoods of severely and moderately cyclone affected communities in the townships of Myebon, Pauktaw, Kyaukpyu and Minbya.

title: Piloting the Cooperative Model in Myanmar
description: The project will begin with an assessment of cooperatives in Myanmar to increase knowledge and understanding of the context and potential to link small scale farmers to markets. It will also follow with awareness raising activities through exchange visits, training and setting up mechanisms for collective services for its members and finally begin the registration process for a sesame trading cooperative.

title: Programme development for building resilience in Delta, Rakhine and Dryzone
description: The project will develop the BRACED resilience programme for Myanmar, to be funded by DFID. During this 6 month period we will generate a deeper understanding of the vulnerability context; develop a stronger, more diverse consortium; develop a strong logframe and MEL framework, and fully design the programme.

title: Strengthening Civil Society in Myanmar
description: Shalom and Paung Ku's central goal is to have empowered strong civil society by facilitating partners to develop and reflect on existing capacity, identifying what resources are needed to build a stable, sustainable and peaceful society based on the self -reliance development approach..  Meetings and workshops will be organized and/or facilitated for partners to access knowledge, lessons learnt and technical resources and giving micro -grant. Shalom Local Development Network initiative shall develop institutional capacity to support current IDPs in camps to empower, for returning and rebuilding of stable and sustainable communities.

title: Empowering the Local CBOs Network for Ensuring Resources Governance in Myanmar
description: The capacity of the Kachin communities who are dependent on forestry and upland agriculture will be strengthened to improve, sustain upland farm productivity and build resilience to climate change. A technically equipped network of skilled trainers supported by a central community nursery service will be created and established.    Community forestry networks will participate in national and sub -national dialogue, supported with evidence -based discussion papers, to strengthen policies and programmes on community forestry. This project provides many potential down -stream benefits and income generation while securing farmland and forest.

title: Capacity building for staff who are working on Kachin livelihood program
description: In the P00928 program, two project MYAB 27 and 30 have been running with OHK's first trench funding support. Unfortunately two project do not enough for capacity building for both staff and project staff. But assessment result is pointing out that need to increase on financial , gender knowledge and reporting. That is why planned in the staff plan. But funding support need to get from this OHK's second trench fund to Myanmar. As this project is directly supporting the capacity activity of staff and partners, scope of this MYAB 35 will be capacity building by attending training/workshop, meeting, visiting other project areas.

title: Myanmar: Gender Transformative & Responsible Agribusiness Investment in SEA
description: The project will cover up to 30 villages in the Kaukphyu area that are going to be impacted by the development of a Special Economic Zone. The project will educate these villagers about their rights through village representatives and it will support other villagers to better understand the potential impacts of the SEZ, participate in the ESIAs and engage constructively with companies on the potential and real impacts of the SEZs on their lives and livelihoods.

title: Emergency WASH and Food Security response to IDPs in Kachin (CIDA-2015/16)
description: Since 2011, Oxfam and its partners have been meeting the needs of over 19,000 Internally Displaced Persons in Kachin in 53 camps (41 camps in GCA and 12 camps in NGCA) through integrated WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) and EFSVL (Emergency Food Security and Vulnerable Livelihoods) programming with partners Kachin Baptist Convention (KBC) and Shalom with funding from ECHO, DFATD, and DFAT, This support is due to end in April 2015.  For this project, Oxfam will additionally be partnering with Metta and SALLOM with whom Oxfam has been partnering with on other projects since 1999. This project is a continuation of the above work to fill the humanitarian gaps in the targeted areas since this is crucial to ensure continuity of the current support to the target populations.   This project will provide critical lifesaving response to 3364 Households IDPs (14,90015795 individuals) in Kachin State. the WASH sector will focus on providing appropriate, sustainable water supply  other WASH facilities and services to 1152 HH  (4735 individuals )vulnerable IDP camps located in the GCA while the Livelihoods part of the project will target 2212 HH (11060, individuals both in the GCA (1331 HH) and NGCA (11,000  individuals (2200 HH), by preventing and reducing the prevalence of malnutrition.

title: Promoting land tenure security through community forestry
description: Increase knowledge of Community forest management plan, facilitate to give wider community forest effects for rural development to both government staff and forest user groups. By having township level and Kachin state level net working groups, raised collective voice for policy influence on land law and community forest instruction. These will result government support land certification to communities who are applying CF certificates. That's why training , excursion and collaboration are not only aim for land tenure security but also will give positive benefit targeted community sustainability  livelihood. Research and IEC (Information, Education and Communication) material will also be made and it will give us gaps we should do in future development of the communities.

title: Tat Lan Food Security and Livelihood Program in Myanamar (Phase II)
description: The project will be implemented in 62 villages: the majority of the project activities support communities to ‘hang -in', empowering them to raise their voices to get their development needs met, and contributing to preparing them to protect their livelihoods and assets as the Special Economic Zone (SEZ) development occurs.  The project also creates evidence to support communities to be able to ‘set out' in the future once the SEZ is developed, by mapping local skills, and researching for examples of good practice industrialization projects that can benefit local communities.  Communities will be empowered to raise their voice to local government actors through the project, evidence from research and information on best practice will be presented at the union level to key stakeholders so that there is a conversation at both levels on investment practices, community development and sustainable livelihoods.

title: Emergency Food Security response for NGCA-Kachin (ECHO)
description: Result 1; focuses on providing essential food needs to the six hard to reach camps in the Non Government Control Areas (NGCA) which are not covered by World Food Programme (WFP) under their food distribution. Food distribution is still the only way to respond to the needs of these target camps. Due to the fact that they are far from any safe local markets and that those camps are small and separated from each other, provision of unconditional cash grants proved to be inefficient and livelihood opportunities remain very limited. In addition, all camps have limitations for large scale gardening due to insufficient space, steep terrain, rocky ground or high elevation. Hence they remain highly dependent on external support for food. The support to food distribution (food aid) for a period of 4 months and 4 months for cash/voucher is anticipated to increase individual/household food intake, diversify households diet and increase the number of meals consumed per day for both households and individual members.  Result 2; seeks to identify alternatives response options ( Cash/Voucher) against continuous food provision for the 9000 people in the six hard to reach camps.

title: Right to Food in Myanmar
description: The Project will be implemented in 90 villages spread across 2 states (Kachin and Shan - Northern Shan and Southern Shan regions). There will be mutually reinforced interventions interspersed through four intermediate country outcomes focusing on building capacity and policy influencing at micro, meso and macro levels. At micro level, the project will work with local community mainly women smallholder farmers, landless, people who have lost their land and livelihoods due to land grabbing and forest dwellers by enhancing their knowledge, awareness rights related to natural resource management, land, community forestry and rights. Community members will be trained on community led advocacy, dispute resolution and engagement with private sector investor. They will also be trained on resource mapping, monitoring impact of various investments in the local areas on the local environment and livelihoods of community. These communities will be collectivised into alliances for greater voice and impact.

title: Towards a localized sustainable livelihood system in Kachin, Myanmar
description: Oxfam will work through 2 partners for the livelihood support including capacity building for small business, policy influence and advocacy, and learning on new areas. For livelihood, providing grants and technical for market and value change to (11) communities in Kachin, especially targeting women will be main activities.   Applying farm land forms (7) and Community Forest certificate, cluster meeting among beneficiaries for sharing and lessons learnt, coordination and advocacy meeting with political parties and Government department will be conducted.  Rapid care analysis and women economic empowerment will be part of pilot learning.

title: Workforce Disclosure Initiative
description: ShareAction and Oxfam collaborate in a 30 month project aimed at driving up the transparency of employment practices and improve the well -being of workers in companies and their supply chains. The project will have a particular focus on people in developing countries that are employed in the supply -chains of large multinational companies, particularly those listed in the ‘FTSE 100'.

title: Land and livelihoods in Kachin State, Myanmar
description: The project is going to work with two partners (ALinn Bamaw and Kachin Conservation Working Group  - KCWG) at 22 villages and 5 Internally Displaced Person (IDP) camps in 5 townships, Kachin state.  The project targeted women and men in that 22 villages and 5 IDP camps to improve their knowledge and skill on their right and access to land and forest. The project is also going to form farmers group and community forest user groups in the villages and applying land registration  and Community Forest certification to secure their land and forest, at the same time improving their livelihoods based on their land and forest. Civil Society Organisation (CSO) networking group would be created by the project partners and local CSOs in Kachin for creating the platform between the government and community group for improving their law and policy discussion on gender, land and forest. The women empowerment and leadership and encouragement of gender on land activities would be implemented by the project for the improvement of women role in land and forest sectors including law and policy.

title: Making desludging works in Kachin State, Myanmar
description: This project will support the desludging service providers in Myitkyina township of Kachin State to maximise their customer base, revenue and profit. This will increase sustainability by reducing or removing the need for external subsidies. By reducing or modifying the role of unregulated service providers, the indiscriminate dumping of waste will be reduced. Further support will be provided to the municipal government by developing an innovative and appropriate design for a sludge treatment site which will further reduce public health risks.

title: Workforce Disclosure Initiative - Restricted Funds - R07119
description: Participate in an advisory group to develop a survey set of questions about a company's workforce (operations and supply chain) that investors will use with investee companies, covering eg wages, employment contract status, women in supervisory roles, membership of a union, etc. Develop 3 case studies based on research and experience to date, of interest to Department for International Development (DFID) and relevant to the project. Develop a further 2 case studies, one in each of Myanmar and Tanzania that illustrate the issues. Stakeholder consultation in each of Myanmar and Tanzania eg via a roundtable or interviews with relevant stakeholders on workers' rights in supply chains relevant to UK investors

title: Strengthening the Livelihoods of Small-Scale Farmers in Nigeria (SLISSFAN)
description: This three -year project aims to improve the livelihoods of 6,000 small -scale farmers in the middle belt and northern parts of Nigeria. The project will work with farmers, government, private sector and parliaments on policy reforms, increased investment and budget performance for better support services and increased agricultural productivity and competitiveness. The project will strengthen advocacy capacities of project partners and beneficiaries to demand accountability from duty bearers and influence policies to respond to needs of farmers. The project is funded by EC and OGB and contributes to objectives under SCO 1.1

title: Advocacy for increased investment on Small-scale agriculture in Nigeria
description: Project aims to operationalise Oxfam's Food Justice campaign supporting food security in Nigeria through recognising and supporting small -scale farmers, advocating for improved quantity and quality of public investment in agriculture, as well as increased women's representation and participation in decision -making at all levels of agricultural governance and production. Value addition will include advocacy and public campaigning, Alliance Building and Networking, capacity building, media engagement and popular mobilisation, for small -scale farmers' organisations, CSOs and organised private sector for campaigns and related activities.

title: Improving Women's Leadership and Effectiveness in the Agricultural Governance
description: Project will support efforts to increase women's leadership and participation in decision -making at all levels of agricultural governance and production through building women's skills and capacity to improve production, income and lead positions in agricultural associations and governance. Action at national, state and local levels and will include in -depth research, knowledge dissemination and support for policy debates that promote fair agricultural legal framework that favours women. It will work with gender advocates, research institutions, women's agricultural machineries and government institutions for change. SCOs 1, 2, 4 and 5.

title: Empowering smallholder farmers against disaster and emergency impacts in Nigeria
description: The project aims to ensure the preparedness of small scale farmers  for the impacts of disasters and emergencies in view of their vulnerability especially women, and limited capacity to recover from such impacts. The project will facilitate processes that will advocate and support relevant movements for policy reforms and the development of intruments to support SHF in the event of disasters and emergencies. The project also aims to build the adapative capacity of farmers to these, while reducing their economic losses from disasters and emergencies and facilitation of public support to them. The project supports SCO 1.1, 4, 5.1

title: Economic Justice Campaign Launch
description: On June 1, 2011 Oxfam will launch a global campaign on Food Justice in a resource - constrained world. The goal of this campaign is to support people living in poverty to claim power in the way the world manages land; water and climate change so that they can grow or buy enough food to eat now and in the future.   In Nigeria the Voices for food security Campaign will participate in launching of this new campaign with a series of events and activities to introduce the new campaign to the public. The campaign partners will use this opportunity to promote the campaign objectives and priorities using new campaign strategies and tools.

title: Engaging the Private Sector in Strengthening Small Scale Agric Sector
description: Oxfam and its partners within its livelihoods and private sector programme plan to host an interactive workshop aimed at bringing small holder farmers and the private sector players together on a platform for shared dialogue and engagement. The project will also identify specific private sector players and create linkages between them and small holder farmers.
