title: Empowering smallholder farmers against disaster and emergency impacts in Nigeria
description: The project aims to ensure the preparedness of small scale farmers  for the impacts of disasters and emergencies in view of their vulnerability especially women, and limited capacity to recover from such impacts. The project will facilitate processes that will advocate and support relevant movements for policy reforms and the development of instruments to support SHF in the event of disasters and emergencies. The project also aims to build the adaptive capacity of farmers to these, while reducing their economic losses from disasters and emergencies and facilitation of public support to them. The project supports SCO 1.1, 4, 5.1

title: Programme Quality and Accountability Enhancement
description: External Consultations with partners and Staff: Engaging an external person to carry out the review is to allow for objective and structured information based on evidence. Programme/Partners Visits: Cross partner Learning and knowledge sharing visits   Country Learning Review: Reflection and learning by programme teams and partners. It provides opportunities for country team to meet with stakeholders in order to review their outputs.   Capacity Building/Knowledge Sharing:Significant Change Stories will be developed to demonstrate how Oxfam and its partners are contributing to fighting poverty.

title: Building Citizen's Movements in Support of the GROW campaign
description: This will be achieved using public campaigning approaches particularly use of Nigerian celebrities, ( musicians and actors) traditional media and digital campaigning tools to reach out to existing movements particularly the youth, and rural women and farmer groups at  National, state and local levels. key activities will include:  working withe Nigerian celebrities, Female Food Hero awards and use of media

title: Advocacy and Campaign for increased investments in SSF agriculture in Nigeria
description: The project seeks to include gendered perspectives in both formal and informal peace processes through the active participation of women in their own right as crucial actors in the establishment of sustainable peace. It will increase the voice and participation of women in decision making on conflict prevention, management and resolution in Nigeria and enable women to address the specific concerns around sexual and gender based violence.

title: Improving Women's leadership & effectiveness in Agriculture in Nigeria.
description: Project will support efforts to increase women's leadership and participation in decision -making at all levels of agricultural governance and production through building women's skills and capacity to improve production, income and lead positions in agricultural associations and governance. Action at national, state and local levels and will include in -depth research, knowledge dissemination and support for policy debates that promote fair agricultural legal framework that favours women. It will work with gender advocates, research institutions, women's agricultural machineries and government institutions for change. SCOs 1, 2, 4 and 5.

title: Global LEAP II
description: 1. An analysis on agricultural budget trend for the past 3 years at the federal level and 2 selected states (Benue and Nasarawa) 2. A network of Civil Society Organisation's/Community Based Organisation's formed and their capacity built to support wider citizens participation; including a network of influential women (comprising of top business women leaders, legislators, governors wives, ministers etc) to advocate on issues affecting small scale women farmers   3. Village/Ward assemblies formed to promote community dialogue around public expenditure and spaces created for them to engage at local, state and federal levels. 4. Human angle/significant change stories developed to show impact of low/increased investment on small scale women farmers especially as it relates to building their resilience to climate change impact. 5. Hold at least one town hall meeting at the state level and one policy dialogue at the federal level on agricultural investments.

title: Women4Women Mobile Platform
description: 1. To develop and test an Information Communication Technicology (ICT) women farmers' information system that incorporates a data collection platform that enables field data collection through self reporting by beneficiaries or through independent enumerators.  2. Trading platform where input suppliers and buyers can be brought together to provide services to farmers  - Extension services, marketing prices, weather information 3. A system that empowers farmers especially women to collect information on their farming needs, track public performance policies (for instance, GES, NIRSAL, Insurance...) 4. Provides GIS services to locate farmers and possibly store and retrieve information about them

title: Engaging the Private Sector in Strengthening  Agric Sector Livelihoods of SSF
description: •Detailed analysis of both sectors interest and challenges in Agribusiness and potential for their engagement at appropriate points in a value chain.•Host relevant interactive workshops aimed at bringing small holder farmers and the private sector players together on a platform to facilitate shared interests and business possibilities.•Identify specific private sector players and small holder farmers with potential for agribusiness collaboration

title: PRO ACT : Building Food Security and Resilience in Northern Nigeria
description: This action focuses on developing resilient livelihoods through integration of humanitarian relief, socioeconomic development, and empowered advocacy as well as improving social protection safety nets and strengthening market system. The action will benefit 35,000 households, of which 50% will be women, through 700 farmer groups and 700 savings groups in 7 Local Government Areas (LGAs) (3 in Kebbi and 4 in Adamawa States). The LGAs in Kebbi in the Northwest are Birnin Kebbi, Jega and Danko/Wasagu covered by Development Exchange Centre (DEC) Bauchi. In Adamawa in the Northeast, the LGAs are Song, Mubi South, Fufore and Guyuk covered by Christian Rural and Urban Development Association of Nigeria (CRUDAN).

title: Global LEAP - Public Finance Accountability in Nigeria
description: 1. An analysis of national and ODA agricultural and Climate Change Association (CCA) investments at the federal level to determine effectiveness of spending in favour of small scale women farmers and improve coordination among donors. 2. Capacity building of farmer and women organisations to follow the money at the local and state levels 3. Documentation of Ogbonge Women impact stories to inform programme planing and fundraising. 4. Production of digital campaign materials – videos, PSA's,  5. Celebrities engagement to include – concerts, media filed visits, advocacy visits to policy makers

title: Ensuring Program Quality & Research for Resilience and Voice for Rural Nigeria
description: This project provides for programme development and management; monitoring, evaluation learning (MEL) and social accountability (SA) as well as generating evidence in support of campaigning, advocacy and influencing in support of Nigerian Oxfam Country Strategy (OCS) ambition. It includes partner capacity building and partnership strengthening as well as compliance. It covers staff costs and overheads, programme coordination involving, and gender related actions. This project ensures coherence between partner plans and overall programme ambition; effective and regular monitoring of progress against the Country OCS; programme quality reviews, and impact assessment.

title: Access to Water and Flexible Financial Services for SSFs
description: •Detailed analysis of both sectors interest and challenges in Agribusiness and potential for their engagement at appropriate points in a value chain.•Host relevant interactive workshops aimed at bringing small holder farmers and the private sector players together on a platform to facilitate shared interests and business possibilities.•Identify specific private sector players and small holder farmers with potential for agribusiness collaboration

title: Innocent - Cash transfers in Gweru , Nigeria ( Oxfam Novib)
description: To meet the basic food needs of families in Gwoza, North East Nigeria (an area which is highly dependent on humanitarian support and is inhabited with relocated Internally Displaced Persons (IDP's)) through provision of unconditional cash transfers.

title: OGB PA Discretionary Contribution to Nigeria FY2018-2019
description: The amount of the discretionary fund will be spent on programmes and the balance will be spent on core costs. The amount going to programme will be added to ONL DF and spent on 3 local partners that are NAWIA, CCDP and YMCA.  Oxfam in Nigeria has 3 local partners in the middle belt of Nigeria in Benue, Nasarawa and Plateau. They have implemented the Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLA) projects funded 100% through unrestricted lines (counterpart) thus far. There is no donor funding involved. They submitted their annual work plan and budget early this fiscal year for the continuation of the project. These three local partners are: 1. NAWIA: the Nigeria Association of Women in Agriculture in Benue 2. CCDP: Cocin Community Development Program in Plateau 3. YMCA: Young (wo)Men's  Christian Association in Narasawa   Together, they have been reaching the past two years 42,702 farmers, 75% of whom are females. Together, they raised $1,800,000 to build start -ups, small (agro allied) businesses and downright farming activities. The plan for April 2018 - March 2019 was to add 22,000 more farmers this fiscal year.

title: PROSELL - PA contribution to Oxfam Novib
description: Oxfam and its partner, Disaster Emergency Committee (DEC), will work jointly to reach target households in order to increase levels of food production, income and capacity to cope with shocks. The approach will strengthen community organisations, enhance their ability to access services, negotiate with local authorities, contribute to policy development, and implement smallholder agriculture.

title: PROACT - PA contribution to Oxfam Novib
description: This project focuses on developing resilient livelihoods through integration of humanitarian relief, socioeconomic development, and empowered advocacy as well as improving social protection/safety nets and strengthening system. The approach provides a coherent framework to achieve the action objective by concurrently addressing short -term targeted agricultural outcomes with improved implementation of government policies and institutional capacity development.   Through support from Oxfam and its partners, Development Exchange Centre (DEC) and Christian Rural and Urban Development Association of Nigeria (CRUDAN), target households will increase capacity to cope with shocks, levels of food production and income. Pro -Resilience Action (PROACT) approach will strengthen community organisations, enhance their ability to access services, negotiate with local authorities, contribute to policy development and implementation on smallholder agriculture.

title: OGB PA Discretionary Contribution to Nigeria FY20 and FY21
description: As above

title: Start Fund - Nigeria Alert 676 - Anticipation of Electoral Violence
description: "In the build -up to the 2023 general elections in a few weeks, the political space has been heated up with ongoing campaigns across the presidential candidates and agitations from their supporters virtually, across social media platforms, and with physical encounters some of which have turned violent     The impact could result in loss of lives and properties, loss of livelihoods for those affected and displacement in extreme cases. People are often caught up in conflict as they start and escalate rather rapidly without measures in place to mitigate, minimise impact or provide immediate relief  We are unable to access funding to prepare for preventive, immediate, and interim response to this potential crisis within this time. However, the availability of the Start Fund will enable us to set preventive steps to enable prompt identification of early warning signs of sudden and escalating election violence to enable an early response and mitigation measures towards curtailing the violence.

title: PROSELL - PA contribution to Oxfam Novib (final yr of NGAA87)
description: Oxfam and its partner, Disaster Emergency Committee (DEC), will work jointly to reach target households in order to increase levels of food production, income and capacity to cope with shocks. The approach will strengthen community organizations, enhance their ability to access services, negotiate with local authorities, contribute to policy development, and implement smallholder agriculture.

title: Valuing Women's Work (VWW) strategy seed funding
description: Supporting the coming together and claiming of rights by coalitions of organisations, channelling resources, connecting and convening across sectors and countries. •Campaigning and influencing for government and private sector policies and practices, such as social protection and leave policies •Offering policy and research expertise and collaboration, in support of southern feminist evidence building •Securing long term core funding for diverse feminist -led alliances in countries, regions and globally •‘Walking the talk' within Oxfam especially in relation to staff policies around care, parental leave, pay for all workers.   And ensuring our supply chain is reflective of our values eg: in our contracts with companies that deliver cleaning, guardian or procurement services

title: Valuing Women's Work PA contributions
description: Project for VWW for PA contributions via OPA's

title: Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) Oxfam Gaza Emergency Response
description: Save lives and facilitate improved access to critical basic services 22,000 to internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and conflict -affected households in the Gaza Strip through the holistic provision of Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) & Non Food Items (NFI), putting the mitigation of protection risks at the centre of the intervention

title: Providing food for poor families in the Gaza Strip
description: The present project strives to increase access to nutritious food and improve the health and wellbeing for 105 families (735 men, women and children).  Projects locations are Gaza city and Khan Younis governorate. Target beneficiaries are women headed households, families with large number of dependents, with members with disabilities and the unemployed.  Activities include chicken breeding for meat and for eggs, backyard and rooftop gardens.  The project will be managed by Oxfam GB; implemented by MA'AN Development Centre in coordination with Food Security and Livelihoods Coordinator, Deputy, project officer and assistants.

title: Enhancing income & food security in the Occupied Palestine Territory
description: This is the Gaza component  of the ECHO proposal. It has CFW and FS activities.   The proposed intervention will implement cash for work (CFW) and Food Security activities (rabbits' breeding and backyard garden production). The CFW will provide a much needed cash injection for 3,031 beneficiaries (433 households) to improve their food consumption, cover other basic needs and to reduce their debts. Through the CFW activities 47Km of Agricultural Roads will be rehabilitated and 25 Schools will be developed.   The FS activities aim to provide longer -term improvement in diet and a raise of income for 3,150 beneficiaries (450 needy households).

title: Enhancing food security in the Occupied Palestine Territory
description: This project is in line with the livelihood strategy and it is contributing to SCO 1 and aims to increase and diversify food and cash income sources of vulnerable households in Jericho, Tubas. It will promote integrated and sustainable farming systems by linking this project with the EDP programme in a context of very limited access to natural resources and markets .The total number of beneficiaries in West Bank is 425 households (approximately 2,805 individuals) who will engage in small -scale agriculture production activities. Oxfam implements the project in partnership with ESDC.

title: Producing and Promoting Fairtrade goods for European Union Markets
description: This project is part of SCO 1 and SCO 3. The objective is to strengthen the food & income security of impoverished populations in Palestine & contribute to the development of a fair trade and organic sector. The specific objective is to enhance the livelihoods of 3,106 farming households (18,636 persons) Oxfam implements the project with the ESDC and NFC. The groups are trained for institutional & capacity building so that they receive Fair -trade & organic certification & can market products internationally.

title: Market Access to Women Producer Cooperatives in the Occupied Palestine Territory
description: This project is part of SCO 1 and SCO 3. This initiative will provide 547 producers (of whom 417 are women) with the working capital, training, cooperative education needed to work collectively to supply the high -end food products needed by NFC for meeting an ever growing demand for high -quality, home -style processed food in local and international market. Simultaneously, it will build the capacity of these cooperatives towards becoming effective and profitable enterprises, while improving the efficiency and competiveness of NFC.

title: Provision of food supplies for vulnerable communties in urban Areas in Gaza
description: A Cash Transfer Pilot for 240 vulnerable households (HH's)in urban Gaza to receive a non -conditional Cash Grant to supplement their HH income to improve their food security situation.  Cash for Work activities for 210 beneficiaries to undertake Community Maintenance Works (including support to Disaster Risk Reduction activities) and to work in Sewing Workshops to produce garments.  The Cash for Work activities will include 2 shifts of 25 days with 2 payments to beneficiaries.  The Cash Transfer Pilot will be closely monitored as a Pilot activity with a learning workshop at the end for interested stakeholders.

title: Cash Voucher (for food ) Distribution- E-Voucher Modality Implementation
description: An Urban voucher Pilot that begun in 2009 and has now been modulated into the E voucher system with same amount of beneficiary households, 2335 around 15 000 thousand beneficiaries in 23 supermarkets in three governorates of the Gaza Strip.

title: Developing a Detailed Road Map for Agribusiness Development in the OPt.
description: Analyzing and identifying the highest potential sub -sectors, products and specific business opportunities to achieve the best impact on pro -poor economic development and growth. The effort will look at best global practices and benchmarks, identify the market system constraints and failures and make concrete recommendations for changes required to enable Palestinian businesses to convert comparative advantage to truly sustainable competitive advantage. The study will pay particular attention to specific opportunities that might produce significant benefits for women and the poorer smallholder farmers supplying these businesses

title: Producing and promoting high quality processed products in West Bank Palestine
description: With support from Foundation TELLUS VIVA more than 16,000 poor farmers will be able to generate a sustainable income by producing and promoting high quality and  fair trade goods to local, national and international markets.  The project will show that the olive paste, thyme (Za'tar), dairy products, fruits and honey that have traditionally been produced and processed in rural communities of Palestine, can match the quality of the local, regional and external high quality (value), fair -trade and organic market and can become a profitable and fair business for economic growth and poverty alleviation.

title: Support to Olive oil farmers & cooperatives in West Bank Palestine
description: This project contributes to SCO 1 and aims to strengthen the food & income security of subsistence and small scale olive farmers in Palestine & contribute to the development of a functioning VC.  Thus small and medium scale farmers in the West Bank have fair and equitable access to commercial markets within a conducive institutional and policy environment. Olive oil farmers of 38 Coops/group and 12 women -only coops will be trained for quality olive oil and olive paste production. The groups are trained for institutional & capacity building so that they receive Fairtrade & organic certification & can market olive oil and paste internationally.

title: Supporting small scale farmers & cooperatives market their produce in West Bank
description: This project  aims to strengthen the food & income security of 1875 subsistence and small scale olive farmers in Palestine & contribute to the development of a functioning VC.  Thus small and medium scale farmers in the West Bank have fair and equitable access to commercial markets within a conducive institutional and policy environment. Olive oil farmers of 38 Coops/group and 12 women -only coops (354 women) will be trained for quality olive oil and olive paste production. The groups are trained for institutional & capacity building so that they receive Fairtrade & organic certification & can market olive oil and paste internationally.

title: Improving children's food security & education in Gaza, Palestine
description: 195 families will have established food production units. 50 out of 195 will be the families supported by OGB in the past and have production units running – they will be provided with additional support required. The rest 145 will establish new production units and will be provided with 300 broilers & other inputs required together with the training. Women from these 145 households will be employed in CFW activities for 1 month: 70 will be cooking meals for kindergarten children and 75 will be employed as seamstresses. Additional 25 families will be chosen for provision of cash grants for establishing small scale businesses

title: Policy & advocacy initiatives support food security & justice in West Bank
description: Support OGB programmes with advocacy and comms work and support the implementation of OI's policy and advocacy strategy.

title: Suppot to olive oil farmers access markets with European Union funds, West Bank
description: This project  aims to strengthen the food & income security of 1295 subsistence and small scale olive farmers in Palestine & contribute to the development of a functioning VC.  Thus small and medium scale farmers in the West Bank have fair and equitable access to commercial markets within a conducive institutional and policy environment. Olive oil farmers of 38 Coops/group and 6 women -only coops (190 women) will be trained for quality olive oil and olive paste production. The groups are trained for institutional & capacity building so that they receive Fairtrade & organic certification & can market olive oil and paste internationally.

title: Cash Voucher Project (E-Voucher)
description: The present project has implied a doubling of the caseload from 15,000 to over 30,000 beneficiaries (c. 5, 600 households)

title: Nutrition knowledge campaign for women in Gaza, Occupied Palestinian Territory
description: The project will provide a range of activities to UVP female beneficiaries to enable them to socialise and develop informal support networks whilst learning about and applying improved practices to support nutritional improvement within their families.  This will be done through a range of activities including practical cooking demonstrations; mobile theatre shows, role play exercises and group activities to highlight and showcase health and nutrition messages; psychosocial support groups; educational visits to food factories/establishments.

title: Cooperative growth & marketing in Jordan Valley, Occupied Palestinian Territory
description: This project  aims to strengthen the income security of 100 small scale fresh vegetable farmers in Palestine (Jordan Valley) & contribute to the development of a functioning fresh vegetable VC.  Thus small scale farmers in the JV have fair and equitable access to commercial markets within a conducive institutional and policy environment. FV farmers of 2 Coops will be supported to increase their profit margin. The coops are supported with two trucks, capacity building and mentoring so that they can market colectively their produce.

title: From Grove to Market-Project Direct
description: For the project 'From grove to Market' to make the olive market work for subsistence and small -scale farmers in the occupied Palestinian territory, and more specifically for small and medium scale farmers from vulnerable and poor households in the West Bank to have fair and equitable access to commercial markets within a conducive institutional and policy environment, resulting in increased food and income security and greater resilience to, and ability to respond to, shocks and disasters.

title: Response to flood victims in Gaza
description: OXFAM GB will give cash transfers to a number of flood victims due to the heavy rains that have taken place in Gaza during the past week.

title: Supporting Vulnerable Communities in Urban Areas of the Gaza Strip
description: OGB and partner MA'AN will provide 50 days of work for public works mainly for men and for mixed groups of unemployed tailors, to attempt to reduce the frequent use of negative coping mechanisms and to improve the food security situation of families in Gaza city and north. OGB will also provide unconditional cash for those beneficiaries unable to work for a period of six months making an effort to referr some of the most needy cases for continuing assistance to the Ministry of Social Affairs and other organisations.

title: Value Based Voucher
description: Provide value based vouchers to over 60,000 beneficiaries (c xx households) to purchase a range of commodities from local shops (46) in the vicinity of beneficiary households in 5 governorates in Gaza in two modalities, the CVP with increased commodities and a combined pilot of 10,000 beneficiaries receiving a reduced value based vouchers and flour. The project will stress support for local economy.

title: Vulnerable HHs have improved their food security situation
description: OGB and partner MA'AN will supporting needy communities through provision of services whilst employing mainly men during  50 days of work for public works to attempt to reduce the frequent use of negative coping mechanisms and to improve the food security situation of families in Gaza city and north. OGB will also provide unconditional cash for those beneficiaries unable to work for a period of six months making an effort to referr some of the most needy cases for continuing assistance to the Ministry of Social Affairs and other organisations.

title: Palestine Green Gold from Producer to Consumer
description: For the project 'Palestine Green Gold from Producer to Consumer' to make the olive market work for subsistence and small -scale farmers in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, and more specifically for small and medium scale farmers from vulnerable and poor households in the West Bank and Gaza strip to have fair and equitable access to commercial markets within a conducive institutional and policy environment, resulting in increased food and income security and greater resilience to, and ability to respond to, shocks and disasters.

title: Emergency support, recovery to sustainable agriculture and resilient livelihoods
description: To provide unconditional cash transfers in coordination with the lowest technical level of Ministry of Social Affairs, to a target group of people who have been identified through the social safety net. Transfers will be done for each individual.

title: Improve Access to Market for Farmers in the West Bank
description: The project facilitates positive connections between subsistence and small -scale farmers and export, import and retail companies in domestic, regional and international markets.  At the policy level Oxfam and partners will network with key governmental structures, NGOs and donor agencies. At the community level, producer groups and cooperatives will connect farmers, encourage economies of scale, promote knowledge dissemination and sharing, and enable joint ownership of project activities to improve produce quality and quantity.

title: Emergency Food Security and Livelihoods Support in the Gaza Strip 2014
description: The project will support conflict displaced people living with host families to have improved access to food.  Two thousand five hundred (2500) selected households will receive 3 -one month food vouchers to cover emergency food needs. (Value of vouchers  GBP 51 X 3months X 2,500 HHs = 382,500 GBP.  Oxfam will conduct cross checking and validation of beneficIaries' lists to identify eligible beneficiary households, distribution of voucher cards, and will conduct post -distribution monitoring at shop and household level.

title: Economic Recovery in the Gaza Strip: Promoting Choice, Resilience and Dignity II
description: To contribute to economic recovery and empowerment of small scale farmers, in particular women by: a. addressing the weaknesses within the market systems; and b. promoting alternative livelihoods and income generating opportunities in the OPT.  To increase participation in user -driven market systems for female and male small and medium -scale producers, processors and entrepreneurs in the Gaza Strip.

title: Value Based Voucher
description: Provide vouchers for around 99,180 individuals to buy food commodities, school uniforms and support for the affected families The voucher is becoming a preferred market channel that provides assistance with dignity and stimulates the local economy

title: Opening Space for enhanced food sec & as rehab mechanism for livelihood recovery
description: To improve food security and enhance resilience of war affected vulnerable families using innovative approach and piloting the well being indicator to measure results. All process will be documented through the action learning as well as pilots will be validated

title: Support to war affected and vulnerable population in Palestine
description: Provide temporary support for the improvement of their food security situation for vulnerable women, men and children from very poor households via CfW and UCT/Increased resilience of targeted communities to shocks through sustained access to protection referral pathway and improved coordination for joint planning and response

title: SIDA Market Development Programme in the West Bank and Gaza
description: The proposed four -year programme will facilitate the development of a market model to attract increased investment into small -scale agriculture and simultaneously improve incomes for women and men small -scale producers, synthesising commercial business development with poverty reduction. With key market actors, the programme will catalyse measures that will systemically change the dynamics of three agricultural sub -sectors with high employment and income potential, and the possibility to benefit nearly 50 -60,000 small -scale producers  (SSPs). By enhancing the competitiveness of the selected sub -sectors, the programme will improve small -farmers' engagement in the local market, and potentially the regional and international markets, directly benefitting farmer groups (producer groups and agricultural cooperatives including women -only cooperatives) as well as other actors in the value -chain, including social enterprises, inputs suppliers, processors, retailers, and agribusiness owners and exporters.

title: Meeting the humanitarian needs of conflict affected vulnerable groups in Gaza
description: Linking relief, recovery and development work through the fresh food vouchers bridging and addressing exclusion issues (on protection, gender and other key vulnerability criteria) from large -scale cash and voucher providers beyond NGOs, with a view to improving aid effectiveness through collaboration and partnerships.

title: Palestinian Farmers Connecting to Markets
description: There is an urgent and critical need to improve the functioning of agricultural markets for the benefit of farmers across the West Bank and the Gaza Strip. This is particularly the case in relation to women and youth, noting that existing employment opportunities are highly inequitable. Despite multiple challenges, the occupied Palestinian territory (oPt) has the potential to establish a vibrant and profitable agricultural sector. In order to implement this project, Oxfam has joined with three leading Palestinian organisations: the Agricultural Development Association (PARC), the Rural Women's Development Society (RWDS), and the Palestinian Livestock Development Centre (PLDC).

title: SIDA Market Development Programme in the West Bank and Gaza
description: This four -year programme, funded by the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (SIDA), will facilitate the development of a market model to attract increased investment into small -scale agriculture and simultaneously improve incomes for women and men small -scale producers, synthesising commercial business development with poverty reduction. With key market actors, the programme will catalyse measures that will systemically change the dynamics of three agricultural sub -sectors with high employment and income potential, and the possibility to benefit nearly 50 -60,000 small -scale producers (SSPs). By enhancing the competitiveness of the selected sub -sectors, the programme will improve small -farmers' engagement in the local market, and potentially the regional and international markets, directly benefiting farmer groups (producer groups and agricultural cooperatives including women -only cooperatives) as well as other actors in the value -chain, including social enterprises, inputs suppliers, processors, retailers, and agribusiness owners and exporters.

title: EU SWIM Reuse of Treated Wastewater for Agriculture Irrigation in Southern Gaza
description: Oxfam and partners, Palestinian Environmental Friends (PEF) and the Palestinian Development Association (PARC), will work to improve the quality of treated wastewater from Rafah treatment plant, to ensure that it is within World Health Organisation (WHO) and Palestinian Water Organisation (PWA) standards for wastewater reuse. Furthermore, farmers and the Rafah Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) operational team will be trained on safe and sustainable approaches for the treatment and reuse of wastewater. Oxfam and PARC will also aim to increase farmer's knowledge and awareness, as well as that of local communities, on wastewater reuse, in order to increase their acceptance and willingness to use treated wastewater for productive purposes.  To ensure long term sustainability of the project, Oxfam will work collaboratively with PWA, Ministry of Agriculture (MOA), Ministry of Health (MOH) and other relevant stakeholders to support the establishment and implementation of a framework for the reuse of treated wastewater

title: ECHO Strengthening Human and Protection Assistance for Vulnerable Populations
description: The humanitarian situation in the Occupied Palestinian Territories is directly correlated to the protracted protection crisis characterized by violations of International Humanitarian Law (IHL) and basic human rights. In Gaza, the ongoing Israeli blockade has severely restricted air, land, and sea access for both goods and the movement of people from the Gaza Strip and has enhanced the geo -political separation between Gaza and the rest of Palestine, and reinforced through the lack of engagement by the international community with authorities in Gaza. In 2014, Gaza experienced mass destruction as a result of the Israeli war, which severely damaged infrastructure and livelihoods, resulted in mass civilian casualties and homelessness. The impacts of this conflict require large -scale support and aid assistance in re -building Gaza. Strengthening Humanitarian and Protection Assistance for Vulnerable Populations in the Gaza Strip aims to address the acute humanitarian needs that are consequences of IHL and International Human Rights (IHR) violations, affecting the most vulnerable communities, by strengthening protection mechanisms and disseminating evidence based advocacy. It will provide protection support to the most vulnerable in Gaza by addressing basic food, cash, and water needs. Key protection issues, such as gender based violence, will be addressed to enhance the overall quality of life in Gaza for the most vulnerable. In addition, preparedness and coordination mechanisms will continue between other organisations and actors. This proposed intervention will support Oxfam's influencing work to address the root causes of the humanitarian crisis in Gaza and the IHL and IHR violations. The action will be undertaken by Oxfam in coordination with Palestinian and Israeli civil society partners, key humanitarian stakeholders, other European Commission Humanitarian Office (ECHO) partners, relevant line ministries and local authorities, and the donor and international comm

title: Economic Recovery in the Gaza Strip: Promoting Choice, Resilience and Dignity II
description: To contribute to economic recovery and empowerment of small scale farmers, in particular women by: a. addressing the weaknesses within the market systems; and b. promoting alternative livelihoods and income generating opportunities in the Occupied Palestinian Territories (OPT).  To increase participation in user -driven market systems for female and male small and medium -scale producers, processors and entrepreneurs in the Gaza Strip.

title: OPT Integrated Market Development Program
description: To contribute to resilient and equitable agricultural growth benefitting small -scale women and  men producers in the Occupied Palestinian Territory (oPt).  To increased access of Small Scale Producers (SSPs) to employment, income and improved opportunities   for   women   and   youth   to   enhance   their influencing power.   To utilize a variety of market development approaches to stimulate changes in three main domains: core and supporting functions; enabling environment; and women's economic empowerment and youth inclusion. Operates at two levels: 1) at the agricultural sector level to address major bottlenecks facing SSPs, 2) at the value chain level to address opportunities and constraints in specific value chains.

title: COVID-19 Response OPT Start Fund
description: The project will utilise the simplest modalities to provide this support through a one time cash assistance through a bank transfer. The project will also provide essential protective items to the 10 cooperatives.  The proposed activities are as follows: 1.  Cash assistance to 123 workers (106 women and 17 men) employed by the women cooperatives and have witnessed the cuts in employment due to the crisis. 2. Cash assistance to 77 GBV women survivors leading livelihoods and IGA actiivties (27 referred from Aisha and 50 implemented earlier with Oxfam and MA'AN) . 3. Cash assistance to 50 vulnerable HHs leading  small livelihood projects through Oxfam and MA'AN support since 2019. 4. Distribution of packages of protective materials to the 10 cooperatives to improve Covid -19 measures through the production process. 6. Distribution of health promotion messages online with a reach of up to 800,000 people in the form of artboards, videos and printouts as per the Risk communications and communications strategy jointly delivered with the Risk communications taskforce led by WHO and UNICEF.

title: Increasing Public Awareness and Responsiveness in the Palestinian Social Protec
description: The unprecedented scale of the COVID -19 pandemic has challenged governments around the world to effectively respond to its economic impacts. In Occupied Palestinian Territories (OPT), the crisis has exposed structural weaknesses in the social protection system, which is fragmented across a wide array of longstanding and project -based programmes.  This action aims to enhance coordination across government and non -governmental actors and initiatives to increase programmatic coherence for multi -year planning and financing strategies, to unlock operational synergies and achieve efficiency gains, and to increase access to the administration for social protection applicant and beneficiary households as well as the general public, particularly among poor and vulnerable populations.   In parallel, it also seeks to increase the shock -responsiveness of the system, to introduce and improve decentralized horizontal coordination mechanisms, and capacitate local officials and civil society representatives on themes of social protection governance and administration, including in times of crisis.

title: Support to children and young people in Gaza'
description: Funding to be used for recreational activities targeting children under our protection and psychosocial support interventions. (100% of target must be Children under the age of 18)   To fund tangible items (game equipment, toys, educational materials, creative play, hygiene items) food and refreshments, transport to events and staff costs related to providing events.   Not to be used for infrastructure rebuilding.

title: Sudan Advocacy and Communications Project
description: This project is part of P00387 that aims to link the South and North Sudan programmes to support advocacy and communications work. This project will focus on building on previous work within OI to develop Sudan Wide Advocacy Strategy for helping to address the poverty and suffering, mainly in the areas of humanitarian response, governance and livelihoods. It is intended to link with Khartoum state and Port Sudan education and micro -finance work as capacity increases. Key areas of intervention to address poverty concerns will be focused on issues of political and economic marginalisation, which are strong areas of focus in Oxfam's programmes.

title: PA Contribution to Somaliland (Sanaag & Sool) via Sida Hum Partnership Agreement
description: In response to food insecurity resulting from protracted drought, the project will support 1,600 beneficiary households  - Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and host community (HC)  - in Sanaag region (El Afwein district) and Sool region (Caynabo and Lasanod districts) to meet their basic food needs in a dignified way through providing them with Cash Transfers for food and Cash based on work they will do to improve the conditions in their communities. 1,360 benefiting households will electronically (via mobile phones) receive three cash transfer rounds valued at USD70 and USD75 in Sanaag and Sool respectively per round, while 240 individuals will participate in Cash -for -Work activities and received USD7 per day for 20 days, allowing them to make dignified choices with the amounts they receive, towards meeting their needs.  Being cash transfers, Oxfam will implement this project directly with community members. The Emergency Food Security and Vulnerable Livelihoods (EFSVL) Advisor and Officer will be closely supported by members of the Monitoring Evaluation and Accountability and Learning (MEAL) team (all based in the country programme in Somaliland) through the project cycle. If there is any need for additional support, these staff can rely on Oxfam's EFSVL Advisor at the Regional Platform and also on support from the Global Humanitarian Team for surge support, if the situation warrants it.

title: Somalia Locust Response
description: Improved locust control mechanisms and capacitate/enable government and local community to minimize negative effects on livelihoods of people affected by desert locust. Reduced impact of desert locust and support early livelihood recovery through provision critical agriculture inputs and livestock fodder

title: Integrated    WASH    and    EFSVL    response    through Sida HPA contributions
description: Overall Project Objective: 43,800 men, women and children living in Sool, Sanaag and Togdheer have integrated immediate access to lifesaving food, Water and Sanitation, and can better cope with the effects of drought and other disasters. Expected Result 1 Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH): 43,800 people (mainly Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and most vulnerable host communities) have access to safe water supply and public health risks are reduced for men, women and children living in IDP settlements and rural areas of Eastern Somaliland

title: Integrated WASH & EFSVL response Jubaland through Sida HPA contributions
description: The main objective of this particular project is to improve food security needs through lifesaving unconditional multipurpose cash, Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) and protection services to 10,390 drought affected vulnerable pastoralists households in Afmadow district of Lower Juba region of Somalia. Expected Result 1: Improve immediate food security needs of 450 households in Afmadow district of Lower Juba affected by severe droughts through unconditional cash transfer. Expected Result 2:Improved access to safe and clean drinking water, sanitation and hygiene for 10,390 vulnerable households in Afmadow district of Lower Juba affected by severe droughts. Expected Result 3:Increased access to protection awareness and available services for 62,340 vulnerable women, girls, boys and men in the target districts

title: Emergency Food, Water and Protection interventions for Drought-affected Populati
description: The Swedish International Development Agency (Sida) Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) will support in scaling up Oxfam's and SADO's emergency drought response across Somalia, particularly in the drought hotspots of Gedo/Jubaland and Sool/Eastern Somaliland.  The focus will be on integrated Food Security, Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) and Protection, targeting 17,910 (3940 Female (under 18), 5731 Female (over 18), 3582 Male (under 18) and 4657 Male (over 18) Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and host communities across the two regions.  The proposed activities will address the acute water and food shortages through multipurpose cash transfers, water trucking, rehabilitation/extension of key water points in IDP camps and the provision of hygiene kits and household solar lights to mitigate protection risks. To ensure the sustainability of our actions, it is planned to rehabilitate and extend crucial water sources in rapidly growing IDP camps which receive new daily arrivals displaced by drought, and to set up public solar streetlights in key areas of IDP settlements to counter protection risks at water points and main streets. Service mapping in target locations will accompany our interventions and link the target communities to existing service providers, supporting the integrated nature of this response.

title: RRM - Integrated WASH, EFSVL and Protection drought and conflict affected respon
description: Provide emergency lifesaving Emergency Food Security Livelihood (EFSL), protection and Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) assistance to conflict and drought affected Internally Displaced Person (IDP) and host communities in Buhoodle district of Togdheer region and Erigavo district of Sanaag region.

title: Ethiopia-Somaliland Cross Border Community Based Drought Risk Management Project
description: This is a cross border project targeting 7,654 households in Galbeed province of Somaliland and Somali Region of Ethiopia. 2,035 households in Allay -baday, Faraweine and Balli -gubadle districts  will be targeted in Somaliland. The project aims to reduce the vulnerability of target communities to drought risks through strengthening community preparedness and early warning, implementing drought -proofing activities and enhancing cross border learning on drought risk management.     The project will be implemented through a local NGO, HAVOYOCO, and will collaborate with relevant government institutions, mainly NERAD.

title: Somaliland Fodder Production and Marketing Project
description: This project (under P00322) is a subcontract with FAO for its Rapid Response Rehabilitation of Rural Livelihoods Project (RRRRL) project funded by the WorldBank. The overall objective of the action is to improve food production capacity through increased access and availability to water and fodder for livestock consumption (related to SCO 1.1). Beneficiaries are 7,000 ago -pastoralist households (42,000 people) in Somaliland. Oxfam GB will supervise project implementation by its partner Havoyoco. Key budget allocations are staff, training, and transport. FAO will procure seeds and tools and supervise the construction of water catchments.

title: Pastoral support project
description: This project will contribute to PIP P00516. Its aim is that pastoralists will better protect their interests and secure their rights. In Somaliland, two complementary objectives must be met: (1) Pastoralists participating effectively in organisations that represent their interests and priorities and (2) Institutions that significantly affect pastoralists' lives become more responsive to their needs. The total number of beneficiaries is 70,000 persons. The project will be implemented by Oxfam Hargeisa Office in collaboration with HAVOYOCO, our local partner. Main expenditure will be on capacity building of the POs.

title: Somalia Emergency public Health Response Project
description: This project aims to improve access to water and sanitation for drought affected populations and IDPs in Togdheer region of Somaliland. Establishing water infrastructure and sanitation facilities, promoting hygiene and sanitation,  and distribution of non -food items are among the key project activities. The project will target a total population 70,000 people in drought stricken rural areas of Togdheer region as well as in IDP camps in Burao town.

title: Emergency drought response in Mogadishu and Afgooye corridor
description: This remittance project will partner with a money transfer (remittance) company to provide essential humanitarian relief to conflict people living in Somalia as per SCO 3. Beneficiaries will receive essential cash grants. The project will pilot partnerships with remittance companies who still have access to parts of Somalia where NGOs no longer have access leading to increased suffering of the vulnerable population. The project will be implemented by the selected remittance company in close partnership with Oxfam who will provide training, technical advice and grants for activities.

title: Somalia Water Sanitation, Hygiene and Integrated Livelihoods Emergency Response
description: This project aims to Reduce vulnerability of Lower Juba IDPs and host community to public health and food security risks of drought and conflict in the target area and assisting 216,914 beneficiaries through intensive labour benefiting from improved water,sanitation and  hygiene promotion 16,200 access Food assistance, short term food security and livelihoods support.The projects will be managed by Oxfam GB and implemented by one partner, WASDA.

title: Community Driven Livelihood and Food Security Initiatives (CLFSI)
description: The project contributes to PIP00635. The project location is L.Juba  region. The beneficiaries are 250, 0000 people (41,667 households)   The expected outcomes are Livelihood and food security for 41, 667 households in 22 priority project sites improved; Food insecurity addressed by 22 empowered community based institutions and structures using alternative ways of working in conflict prone areas. The project is managed by Oxfam in cooperation with WASDA and the community. Expenditure is mainly on Cash transfer, Management and Partner Support Costs.

title: EMERGENCY RELIEF IN LOWER SHABELLE AND MOGADISHU
description: A humanitarian assistance project assisting approximately 327,000 (237,000 in Afgooye and 90,000 in Mogadishu) conflict affected IDPs and host communities in Lower Shabelle and Mogadishu. The intervention focuses on provision of safe water, sanitation facilities and hygiene promotion along with emergency livelihoods support (emergency food vouchers, cash relief and labour intensive  - cash for work). It also seeks to provide IDP skills training. Specific attention is paid to the rights and needs of women. The programme also addresses policy and advocacy issues. Oxfam GB will implement it in partnership with Hijra a local NGO based in Somalia.

title: Drought Crisis Response
description: More resources needed for  priority areas of Lower Juba, where we will increase our caseload from 160,000 to 250,000 beneficiaries. Short term interventions include Construction and rehabilitation of boreholes and other water systems; water vouchers; cash distribution; and rehabilitation of transit sites for displaced people.Long -term interventions include de -silting of water pans (birkads); rehabilitation of irrigation systems; pasture regeneration; and seed distribution (dependent on Autumn rains).The projects will be managed by Oxfam GB and implemented by one partner,namely WASDA  .

title: Ethiopia-Somaliland Cross Border Community Based Drought Risk Management Project
description: This is a cross border project targeting 7,654 households in Galbeed province of Somaliland and Somali Region of Ethiopia. 2,035 households in Allay -baday, Faraweine and Balli -gubadle districts  will be targeted in Somaliland. The project aims to reduce the vulnerability of target communities to drought risks through strengthening community preparedness and early warning, implementing drought -proofing activities and enhancing cross border learning on drought risk management.

title: Emergency Response for Drought affected & transit IDPs in Gedo Region, S.Somalia
description: This project aims to Reduce vulnerability of Gedo IDPs and host community to  700,000 displaced people with improved access to water, sanitation and health messaging and 97,450 people with the means to buy food, healthcare and other items that will save lives and help sustain their livelihoods.The projects will be managed by Oxfam GB and implemented by three partners,namely NAPAD,Berdera water committee & SOMA -ACTION .

title: Somaliland Livestock Value chain Review and Synthesis
description: The sudy wll inform how investments should be targeted  in the livestock sector

title: French Embassy Food Aid
description: Oxfam GB will  target communities which will cushion them from drought effects through food access and income support to improve the purchasing power of the households. This will be done through the distribution of food through food voucher, cash for work  in de -silting water sources mainly water pans for preparedness for the next dry season beginning July. The cash relief will be for 500 households who do not have a labourer for the cash for work. Key activities include:  - Multipurpose cash to 400 households for two months in one go following cash working group's recommended transfer value of 130 USD/Household/month.    - Emergency water supply for 6000 people for 30 days following Sphere Standards and WASH Cluster guidelines and using cash/voucher -based modality in consultation with private sector, authorities and communities.    - Hygiene kits distribution to 1,000 households using standard household hygiene kit content and quality recommended by WASH Cluster based on locally adopted items and specification guided by Sphere Standards.   - Hygiene promotion in targeted 6 locations using public health risk reduction approach by employing range of media – including community volunteers, community level committees, opinion leaders, information, education and communication material and mass media to reach estimated 10,000 individuals – including at high -risk population like families with children under five, elderly, people with chronical illnesses, pregnant and breastfeeding women and adolescents.   - 50 cases mainly targeting survivors of gender -based violence (GBV) and individuals facing immediate protection risks will be assisted through cash for protection modality.   - Dissemination of lifesaving protection messages on GBV, child protection, and rights awareness in targeted 6 locations – including directly engaging community volunteers for targeted risk communication and community engagement.

title: Start Ready Risk Pool 4 Drought AA Southern Mudug Somalia
description: "Mudug region, including Galkayo South, is experiencing a rapidly worsening drought that is already increasing displacement pressure; however, it has not yet reached a point of irreversible, large -scale movement into formal Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camps within the targeted areas. Consecutive rainfall failures—including the poor 2024 Deyr, the failure of the 2025 Deyr rains, and forecasts of below -average Gu' 2025 rains—have severely depleted pasture and water sources, weakened livestock, and reduced household purchasing power. In response, some pastoral households have begun short -distance, temporary movement toward peri -urban villages such as Sadex -Higlo, Docol, Laankadawo, Duqaaqo, and Laasacadale in search of water, food, and basic services.  Crucially, local authorities and community leaders confirm that most affected households are still residing with relatives or host communities, rather than relocating to established IDP camps. This indicates that the displacement process is at an early and potentially reversible stage, where timely anticipatory action can still stabilize households and reduce the likelihood of onward movement into camps. At this point, displacement is primarily driven by progressive livelihood erosion, water scarcity, and food insecurity, rather than sudden conflict or catastrophic shocks, making preventive support both feasible and appropriate.  The proposed project is therefore well -timed to address the key push factors before they reach a tipping point. Cash -based assistance will enable households to meet immediate food and essential needs, reduce reliance on debt, and preserve remaining livelihood assets, while water source rehabilitation and emergency water support will ease acute water stress and reduce the need for families to move closer to unreliable water points. Complementary protection interventions will address heightened risks faced by women and girls during water collection and household movement.  As the Jil
